Fast... and not in a good way. In both times I've played it it felt like it was over before any real decisions were made, I felt like just running around a map trying to stop random events that you already knew were happening. 
"Ok I'm going to London to stop the disease from spreading", but no, France already burst into flames because you were someplace else.
A good cooperative game builds its momentum to a place where you think you can have it all and in that moment you either go down and loose horribly or win the game in a massive burst of happiness, this game lacks closure. It reaches to the point I'm barely taking things seriously (about 30 minutes into the game) and then it ends abruptely. 

Sorry Santa, this game makes me want to play Lord of the Rings...

I maaay change my rating, because maybe this is one of those games that are interesting after a series of games (like Shogun for me, I found it interesting after the second play). I'll keep playing it...

Edit: Played it two more times and it got a little better with 4 players. I'll play more to investigate.

Edit: Played more. Won once and it was OK. A 7 is fair...
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Update 2:
This game needs a certain crowd. After playing a two player game. My opponent said he would like to play in teams against each other???  
Clearly this is no such game. If you don't like games where the object is that of defeating the game. Stay away. If you do like such type of games it is one of the best.



Update: Played for a third time a 3P game
What a difference a little rule can make.
I rated it before a 7 (it felt like a 6 but I knew something was wrong)
Upgraded it to an 8.


Important epidemic take the bottom card from the draw pile.


First two games.
Played one rule wrong. In order to eradicate disease you have to go to cities with cubes of that disease an treat them. The action of treating will take one action. So a player can eradicate disease in 2 towns in one turn.
the medic only has to visit the city to automatically cure the disease once when the cure has been found. This works well with the dispatcher.


Only when the final cure is found there is no need for eradication. You win the game automatically.

There is an excellent one page summary of the rules made by Universal head to be found here.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Playing a cooperative game was a cool experience - as it was the first of its sort for me. This had a very cool mechanic in the "intensify" - where you just reshuffle the cards that have already been drawn and add them to the top of the deck, causing already infected locations to well, intensify.

Not always a consistent challenge, sometimes the game simply decided to break you, with no opportunity to salvage the game after even the first or second turn, other times it rolled up and let you run away with an easy victory. For the most part however, it takes some thought to have a shot at winning - you have to manage your risk level, too conservative and you run out of time, too aggressive and you end up burning out on the outbreak track.

Very simple rules, but also a bit too quick to figure out, and the reward for trying to analyse further (which is kind of fun, since you are doing it as a group) isn't always there since you are talking small percentages (in terms of win / loss %). Played it like 8 - 9 times, which is fine, but then it was a toss-up between getting expansions or ridding myself off it and I did the latter.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: First time playing the co-op mechanic.  I found this game's theme to be compelling although the game overall did not blow me away.  The common complaint about the "Dominating Leader" is very appropriate, I feel, as I was just learning the rules for the first time, yet had an experienced player on my team.  Of course, the experienced player eventually took over, telling the other two newbies (including myself) where to go, etc. This robbed me of a very important aspect of a game - the learning process.  Ideally, games should have enough depth that the ideal strategies are not immediately apparent - they should be discovered only after many, many plays.  This gives the player "Eureka!" moments that are extremely satisfying and build a love for that particular game.  Unfortunately, what I'd heard from veteran players is that the ideal strategy to the game is not too hard to figure out, so replayability is limited for me if I ever play with experienced players.  However, I do respect the game because the premise of co-op has layed the groundwork for future game designs, and it has a very original theme in and of itself.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: What I can say about it: it is hard to understand, takes a long time and makes you think twice until making a move. So, let me explain a little more about this game. Usually, if you want to play pandemic for the first time, play with 4 epidemics and if possible, with a person that already played the game at least once. To be sure that you have a chance for the first time, you can take also your characters because in 2, it's even harder, not necessary in 4. Don't forget about the 7 cards in the hand, it's very important. Look at the game and search for cities that have already 3 cubes on them, you don't want explosions or other infections. Look at the infection deck, remember what cities were infected earlier, what have 2-3 cubes on the table, etc. Read the small rule card that every player has in case you forgot something (usually for transport). It usually takes more then 1h - in case is you play for the first time. Try to find cures, don't eradicate them if you don't have time or cards. I think it's the best game that i have played ever on this idea of cooperative playing. For sure i will take an expansion on it :).
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
A classic coop and a must-try for the newcomers!

[b]/update:[/b] It used to be an "8" back in the day, but it has dropped to a 7 for me over the years. And it won't be easy to go back to this version of Pandemic after playing Pandemic Legacy. It is "too basic" and doesn't have that much to offer when compared to its bigger brother. It's a good game, but now I feel that it requires some expansions in order to stay fresh and interesting. The core gameplay loop feels a bit boring and repetitive to me these days to be honest (from a gamers' perspective Spirit Island just kills Pandemic).

Still, if you've never played Pandemic Legacy you should enjoy this basic version of Pandemic quite a bit. It's a cool co-op game with simple rules and involving gameplay (especially for more casual players). The theme comes through really nicely. I strongly suggest playing with 4 players - this game is all about teamplay and table talk, therefore it loses a lot of charm when played only with 2.

Even though it's only a 7 for me right now I will always wholeheartedly recommend it, it's just how I feel about it personally at this point.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Very fun cooperative game in which four diseases can, depending on card draws, very quickly get out of control and send the game 'south' in a hurry. This plays up to 4 people, although as a cooperative game it can easily accommodate 8 if they play as four teams. Players can adjust the degree of difficulty by including 4, 5 or 6 infection cards in the deck. Having the ability to plan ahead and be able to see a few moves ahead in a cooperative context can make a lot of difference. 

Having already owned and played the same designer's similar but less complicated "Forbidden Island," I didn't find "Pandemic" particularly difficult to learn, and, with a handle on the rules, felt I could also easily teach it. However, that comment comes in the context of having rewritten the rules down to a one-page sheet after hours of viewing video and reading through rules forums to get everything clear.  One look through the forums section on BGG will show just how many questions there are about the rules. 

The artwork in this game is beautiful. 

Purchased new for 25% off at local Target, December 2013. I own the 2012 2nd Edition.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is such a addictive coop game! One of the best coop games ever.

I love how the game is set up differently each time, we had games that finished quickly because the game started with the infected cities so close to each other combined with the unfortunate draw of a epidemic card in our second turn. We ended up failing during the first few turns. And then other times our turn/move plans and card draws went so well that we beat the game in only half of what a normal game would take. 

Luck is major factor in gameplay but it is what it is, I like to think that's just how a real world epidemic would have played out. This doesn't diminish how fun this game is, careful planning with minimal wasted move definitely works fine if the cards are not too too bad.

Really love the fact that all players work together to beat a game. So satisfying when flipping over that last vassel and cheers to victory together!

The components and the graphic design are great as well, it's a must have for any modern board gamers.

(Owned Pandemic base game and "On the Brink" expansion. Looking to get some other expansion in the future.)
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
While I do wonder about longevity, this is a good looking game, and almost anyone can join in and feel comfortable from the start. The lack of competition helps this, of course. This is a cooperative game that doesn't require your being comfortable with obscure mythos, sci-fi (Battlestar Galactica), zombies or gnomes. It has a theme that ordinary people at least understand. 

It is also not so complex that new players need to be told what to do all the time, without their understanding what it is that they are doing, or why they should be doing it. I love Arkham Horror, but suggesting that your sweet aunt Mathilda fight the Dimensional Shambler (not even going into the bonuses she receives for having a +6 Sword of Smiting) while you go through a gate to another world is quite different to suggesting that she catch a shuttle flight to Sydney to cure the red disease. Yes, I know, I shouldn't be playing Arkham Horror with aunt Mathila in the first place, but Pandemic allows you to play with (almost) anyone, with a fair chance that they actually enjoy themselves. That makes it a must have in my collection.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
As a cooperative game with perfect information of other players' status and semi-predictable random events, it really encourages strong personalities to dominate the game, making the other players merely their agents. The game balance requires carefully coordinated planning - encouraging analytical or experienced players to make that problem worse with detailed "advice" for less experienced players. I'm pretty bad about that myself.

Most of the loss conditions don't really feel like "failures" within the theme of the game, which some people find annoying; others continually feel they were "so close" and keep trying. (Though often those games only feel "close" because of the theme, not in terms of game mechanics.)

There is a *LOT* of randomness in the initial shuffle, though by 1/4 of the way into the game half of the randomness gets pretty predictable. I'd estimate only ~10% of the shuffles are impossible to win, but many more might only be /likely/ to be won by someone with knowledge of the draw decks (in particular which cards will be unplayable since they are near the bottom of the player draw pile).
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
There are times I play Pandemic and it feels like a perfect 10 game. There are times I play Pandemic and it feels like a 4 game, and that's my quandary with the game... It is entirely group dependent. 

In Pandemic all players information is open (even if your cards are hidden, everyone can communicate what they have), this makes it easy for a vocal headstrong leader of the group to take over and to tell everyone what do do. It is easy for a player lacking confidence to never make a decision and to ask others to tell them what to do. When these things happen the game struggles. 

However, when you find a group where everyone is working together and problem solving and offering input... the game is a masterpiece. It can feel like you and your squad are a well oiled machine going up against an equally tricky game. Sometimes losing seems unfair and winning seems lucky, but when the group works well, you always want to play again.

That's my trouble with this game, in some groups I always want to play this game, while in others I try to avoid it at all costs. The game is brilliant, but the people can ruin it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is the game that got me into the hobby, so a large part of my perfect rating for this game has to do with nostalgia of discovering this game together with my wife and all the memories that came with it. That said, the game has a perfect design to it, and the theme really draws you in. Every decision you make feels very important; it leaves your group talking about how you could've done things differently after the game and makes you immediately want to play it again. This is the perfect gateway game that shows the power of what tabletop games can do. I honestly cannot recommend this game enough for people getting into board games. 

That being said..... I don't feel any urge to play this now that the world is experiencing an actual pandemic. Sure, an argument could be made that maybe some people would like playing a game where they can "beat" the pandemic, but I'd rather play a game that doesn't talk about the thing devastating the whole world right now. I'll still hang onto it though, hoping that someday there will be a time that it doesn't feel so weird and sad. 

-On the Brink expansion added.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Full disclosure, I really don't like cooperative games. It's not because I am super competitive, but because it is very easy for one person to take the reigns of the game and dominate the decisions (aka quarterbacking). Despite this, Pandemic is an absolutely amazing co-op game. The asymmetrical player powers make for some really fun combos that can be pretty satisfying. But the best thing about this game is the tension that is created. You really feel like there is an imminent threat with the viruses wiping out the planet. Adding the virus cubes onto the board makes everyone more and more nervous as the game progresses. It is just incredible that a game can create such a sense of pending dread. 

It might just be me, but for some reason I feel that the game is very much predetermined. Every turn there seems to be an optimal move that should be taken, regardless of whose turn it is. "Oh based on this, I clearly should go over here and clean up the red virus." There isn't really a feeling that there are pros and cons to each decision you make so it feels much more scripted than I'd like.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Fun cooperative game with great mechanics to control the villain element of the game - the diseases.  The variable player powers add a lot to the game and it is genuinely cooperative, you actually work together, as opposed to games where you all work towards the same goal completely seperately. As an occasional play I think it is probably a big winner but isn't something I am going to want to play very often.

I actually think the rating will probably go down as I play it more.  The more proficient you are at maximizing the efficiency of your turn the less interesting the gameplay is going to be and unlike other games where you will butt heads with other proficient players in this one you will just be agreeing with each other on what everyone should do.  After a while the game will almost play itself and your chances of success will depend entirely on the draw of the cards and how many epidemics you are playing with.  

After many plays, it is starting to feel a little autopilot.  Still a good game but not something I want to buy.  It doesn't have a lot of depth but it is a fun game.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: A very clever game that plays quickly, yet offers relatively deep gameplay.  The tension in this game consistently ratchets up in a manner that provides a great narrative and story arc to the game.  The rules are easy to grasp and the theme is compelling, which makes Pandemic accessible to a wide audience.  There are very few downsides to this game that I can see at the moment; perhaps with repeated play this will become somewhat tired, but there are many combinations of roles to play, each combination providing a different experience requiring changes in approach, tactics and strategy.  I have felt that as I play more I have gotten better at the game, which suggests that this is a game of some skill that can be developed as one discovers how the game reacts and the uses of the various roles.  Highly recommended.  Review based on approximately 15 plays.  Note:  finally beat Heroic level in 2-player with Medic and Researcher - a very powerful combination.  With a different combination (especially excluding the Medic in 2-player), Heroic level will chew you up and spit you out.  Good fun.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
UPDATE2: On the Brink really did breath life into this, and the adjustable difficulty really keeps things interesting too. 2-player is also surprisingly fun, even when playing with just two roles.

----

UPDATE: Still enjoy the odd game of this. Tweaking the challenge level and using the added twists in On the Brink is fun. It works unexpectedly well as a two player game, since it makes sure you'll always be involved in the discussion of what to do next. The role-switch event card also becomes a lot more important and interesting.

----

The shine may be coming off this one. It's neat watching the diseases grow and putting out fire, but it may be a case of luck dominating the game once the basic set of necessary actions to take is figured out. Might turn around on this if some kind of deeper play is evidenced in future games. But the artificially separated cooperative element is also holding it back. Maybe there needs to be a better mechanic than "you can tell everyone what cards you have, without limit, but you just can't show them". Perhaps you can show one face-up card and that's it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
It’s a good cooperative game. It has some good game play
	• everyone is involved 
	• replayability is good
	• there are many ways to win
	• its challenging
The downside is that it starts slow. Especially if you are having to stop and read the rules over and over. Controlling the diseases at first seems too simple and arbitrary. Some people, like Walker, have lots of good ideas how to attack the disease. If a player isn't getting the hang of it they can feel like they are just being told what to do and may lose interest. 

Just when you decide you don't like the game, there are several outbreaks and suddenly you lose -leaving you with the desire to play again. It turns out that its hard to beat the game even in its easiest configuration. 

I figure that if we play the game routinely enough we'll keep the rules fresh in our minds and will enjoy the game more. 

Oddly, the goal is to avoid outbreaks but the outbreaks add excitement to the game. When I play I secretly hope for outbreaks. 

The overall experience is that I don't actually look forward to playing it but I enjoy it when I do.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Some weird things happened to us in this game. We played this with three players six times so far. 

First three times were relatively easy wins. Is this game perhaps too easy? The fourth time we played too slowly and only won on the last possible action of the last player before we would have lost (for lack of cards to draw). Pfff... close one! Is the game finally teaching us a lesson?

Hilariously, we then played our fifth time, all three of us drawing an Epidemy on our first turn, so that at the end of the first round... all having played just once... it was game over already, since we ran into our eighth Outbreak... (with more Outbreaks actually coming in, had the game not ended there). Ouch! So unfair! Was this a case of exceptionally bad RNG? Wondering how rare this occurence really is, it would seem bound to happen every now and then... Game six we then won as we had done the first three times.

Having hit both the highest (game 4) and the lowest (game 5) possible, back to back, I still rate this game not higher than I do, since coop games just don't satisfy my competitive needs.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This game just keeps getting better and better for me.
Possibly the most engaging game I've ever played.
This game really encourages group discussion and interaction. Yes this can sometimes cause the issue of 'Alpha gaming' where one person dominates and takes over, but if you have a decent group this shouldn't be an issue. (Its ok to lose, infact sometimes it makes for a more climactic ending)
My main issue of the game is this games enjoyment comes down to whether the other players are engaged or not. For some people, this game just isn't their style, and they cant get into it. And that can have an effect of the enjoyment for the other players at the table. On the other side of the coin, if you play with a team that really gets into it, It can make it a really memorable experience for everyone. 
Replayability is high, as different infect cards will come out every time, causing different problems to overcome.
Overall, with the right group this game can make for an amazing experience. Highly recommended.

Components: 8/10
Replayability: 8/10
Theme: 8/10
Interaction: 9.5/10
Strategy: 8/10
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: I really don't know why people love this game so much. I find it pretty underwhelming. First off the player(s) that have played before pretty much have to tell new players what to do, so the new players are just extra hands at first. Second, I'm just not afraid of cubes spreading and don't know why we just don't call this a game of set collection, with maybe a loop or two. I can't see why we don't ignore the outbreaks for the most part and just focus on set collection, since that is winning the game mechanic. Finally, had I realized the game would end with the deck, I simply would have asked for the total number of cards in play and divided by the number of players, so people would know the exact number of turns available to collect the card sets. I can see how this would have limited interest as a solo-play game, but it just doesn't grab me like it does so many others in my game group. It may partly be the theme, but it is also the game mechanics - I don't really like Forbidden Island either, which I understand is by the same designer and has the same sort of feel only a lot shorter.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
The first modern board game I've played, and its still my undeniable favourite. It does so many things right. The simple, streamlined design and rules, the slow build-up of tension (with sudden moments of outright panic when Epidemic cards appear), the player powers which are all really strong and make you strategise differently, the absurdly fantastic game balance which often brings games down to the wire... I could go on. This is a masterpiece of game design and its one of the few extremely-well-known titles that absolutely deserves its success.


Side note: I had a rather serious issue with the expansions for this game. The backs of the cards had faded colour, making them impossible to use without putting everything in opaque sleeves. Asmodee told me this meets their quality standards and they would not address the issue. I strongly considered whether to factor this into the review, but decided not to since it has nothing to do with the base game on its own. But I wanted to make a note of it here anyway because its a terrible business practice and they need to be called out for it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: A Great Gateway game for a multitude of reason into both the hobby and the co-op genre. Co-ops in general make great gateway games because new players are able to be coached along because of the win or lose altogether mechanic, but this game takes the cake. This game is easy to teach and learn because the concept is based in our present day and easy for people to grasp and relate to. The game setups up easily and provides clear instructions for new players to follow. With in mere turns anyone can grasp the game and start making decision for them selves and contributing to the outcome. This game also has a relatively short play time which is always a plus when introducing new player to the hobby or gaming in general for non-gamers. Me and my wife being avid co-op players do not find this game to be much of a challenge but it is a nice escape from some of the more stress inducing mind bender co-ops that we play. I rate this game so highly simply because of its utility as a Gateway game for which it fires on all cylinders. Also this game is readily available via major shopping chains.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
We played this out of the box, first time, and remarkably won ... yes, on easy mode and that's not a bad thing for a game like this which has a tremendous amount of ways to lose - and only a few different ways to win. Pandemic is a wonderful cooperative game that we played two-player ... and it's immersive, a little complex at first with all the things happening - but once you get the dynamics down, it's a challenge to meet the conditions towards victory. It's tough though - and we nearly lost it a few times. The game keeps you up on your toes as you try to keep an outbreak from happening. You maneuver your team to various places on the map to help find a cure - while trying not to run out of cards in the process. 

We're definitely interested in the Legacy versions of Pandemic - as we hear it adds a lot to the game play. An ongoing game - even after you play it once, it carries over to other times you play - which is an interesting game mechanism we have yet to explore. Challenging but an incredibly fun game - even if you lose - you ultimately give it your best shot!!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: I feel like this game helped me get into board gaming. I bought it on Black Friday (Full price though LOL), and was fascinated by the Co-op aspect of it. Needless to say, I played it as soon as I could. It wasn't nearly as complicated as we thought it was, and won almost all our games. We DID find out that we were doing a rule incorrectly, which brought our win ratio down, but still won a lot of games. Recently, I won two back-to-back games on the hardest official difficulty. I guess we have to increase the infection counter next time. The first time we played was a blast, the second time was still pretty darn good. I just dislike how short the game feels with a decent amount of setup and space it takes. Also, the theme is lackluster, and doesn't impress a lot of people. The role cards are great, the components are nice, but overall I feel like this game just doesn't have enough for me. I can see why others praise this game so much though. It's a shame that the base game doesn't allow for more players; I don't think I will buy expansions for this anytime soon.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is the king of the coop games. Very nicely made game, with great theme and cool components. The only downside is that i don't like coops. The alfa player try to solve the whole puzzle alone and this goes on all the time. I'm sorry but i'm baised and i want to make the best choices by myself. I see great replayability because every game is different and i believe this game has a great price / value. After a few more games with the right group i started to fall in love with this game. The rules are quite easy, but to beat the game is hard as hell. It is so intense, but it lets you believe that you always have a slight chance to win after all. It is so elegant and encourages clever play!

Pros / Cons:
-If you like coops, this game might be interesting to you.
-Great replayability.
-Great price / value.
-Elegant gameplay with easy rules but with deep meaningful choices.

-If you don't like coops you will start to hate them.
-The alfa will be playing alone and you will be just moving your piece on the board while at the same time moving some cubes up and down.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I'm not sure why people are posting comments about this game being too easy... an easy way to scale it a little tougher, and one of the first rules we implemented, was that you could only discover a cure in a research center of that disease's color, rather than any research center. This requires you to build more stations than simply relying on the one in Atlanta, as well as pulls a bit more strategy into the game. 
Still trying to work out some kinks in the way that sharing knowledge works in the game... allowing players to only share the types of cards they have (ex. "I have 3 red, 1 blue, and 1 special"), and list no city names to other players seems to work fairly well, except that it makes the sharing knowledge action, which is already very difficult, even harder (unless you are the researcher).
The fact that it is a cooperative game is a nice change of pace however, and encourages you to try to play until you beat the game. Works best in groups who have self control and are able to discuss strategies as a group without trying to dictate others moves.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic maintains a sense of urgency in the face of growing crisis, and demands closely managed risk.  But you can't control everything, and there's a good chance it will all unravel before the game ends.

Having previously played Forbidden Island, Pandemic plays very naturally as the obvious parent.  Hand management, infection and epidemics have near replicas in Forbidden Island, while outbreaks progress in an obvious (if scary) way.

In Forbidden Island the game mechanisms match the theme - aided by it being an obviously contrived world.  In contrast, landing Pandemic in the modern world suggests a simulation, which it still could be if your knowledge of disease ends in high school and the evening news.

Play is abstracted from CDC operations to the point where the theme feels pasted-on, and you could just as easily be stomping terrorist insurgencies, mitigating the spread of refugees, holding back the collapse of the banking system, or delaying any other clustered anomaly.  This shouldn't detract from the game - unless you're playing it for the theme.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: :sugar: :) :D :D :D The only co-op or semi-co-op game I've ever really enjoyed, unless you want to torture the definition of semi-co-op almost beyond recognition in order to include Republic of Rome, and quite possibly the greatest gateway game ever invented.  Pandemic is extremely lean in terms of rules and smartly designed to deliver a tough but not unfair challenge, plays quickly, and is almost as much fun as a rehash as it is play experience. More than any other type of game I know (with the possible exception of party games), co-ops require the right crowd to be fun, so one hallmark of a good co-op is that it's highly adaptable. Pandemic has this in spades -- it's easy enough to learn that you can teach it to people who aren't gamers by nature but are people you enjoy spending time with (my wife and parents were enchanted by it when I brought it home last Christmas), and it's hard enough to win that gamers won't scoff at it as child's play. I totally get skepticism as a default approach to co-ops, but this is one that should get a respectful look.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I see now, why it was so easy for us to defeat the game. We made one of the common mistakes. But I expicitly asked whether I'd have to get rid of my cards exceeding 7 right away or after my turn. The way we played it I was able to find the antidote for two diseases in one turn (playing the scientist) Good components, awesome because truely different theme - hey, it's mankind which is on the brink of extinction so you better get yourself together, a lot of interaction. I want this and I want to play it again. Badly! 

Have played it several times now and the fun/time/theme-ratio of this game is one of the best among all games I've yet seen. It takes about 45 minutes to play, 15 minutes to teach and it's a very tense experience. 

Today we played the supermegaheroic level of the game. We intended to play with 5 cards, cause we couldn't find the sixth epidemic card, so I figured it was lost. We build 5 stacks and gamed on, but the sixth card was still in the player cards pile ... Man, did we lose, because of drawing 3 epidemic cards almost in a row.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I really enjoy this game, but fear that it often turns into one person basically taking control of the game, due to its cooperative nature.  As I'm often that one person, it's something I'm a little sensitive to, because I don't want me dictating what everyone should do to ruin the gaming experience of other people that are playing.  I don't think this has happened, but I see the potential that it could.

I like that this game constantly feels on edge, where you always feel like you are a step behind, and disaster could strike at any moment.  The theme is really beautifully implemented in the mechanics of the game.

UPDATE: I lowered from an 8 to a 7 primarily because most games I have played have turned in to one person dictating the game to everyone else, who mostly nods in agreement.  I know this is a common problems with cooperative games, but it seems to happen here even more than usual.  To me this really highlights the importance of mixing things up with a possible traitor/cylon, it keeps everyone on their toes and gets them involved more.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is one of those games that I enjoy more for the cleverness of the design than the actual gameplay. Don't get me wrong, I do think it's fun. I just feel that it is more of a puzzle than a game and that winning or losing is often as much of a function of the randomized deck or the order of roles as it is of playing well. Normally this would turn me off, but I am truly impressed by the innovative mechanisms that drive the game. Stacking the discard pile on top of the draw pile to intensify disease outbreaks as the game goes on and having the outbreaks that are left untreated start to cascade around the world map is both an ingenious idea that add loads of tension and excitement to what is otherwise a pretty dull set collection game.

I'm not sure how well it will hold up to repeated play, as it seems to me that once everyone at the table knows what they are doing, the game will sort of play itself. Like solitaire, winning or losing will probably have already been determined by the shuffle.

Amazing design though...Hats off to Matt Leacock.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Played once, a 3 player game on 'easy'.  While there are clever mechanics here that quite nicely simulate the spread of a disease and the game design can be quite challenging, it does not feel like playing a game, nor quite like a puzzle.  You are not pitting your wits against a sentient thing, as in an opponent in a regular board game or against an AI in a computer game, both of which are much more satisfying.  No, here you are playing against Fate, who delivers its moves through a semi-random card draw (I say semi-random, as there are mechanics in the game to make the same cities come up again).  All you can do is play your hand as dealt the best you can and it is not superior play in overcoming an opponent that allows you to win but random fortune.  And although there is a nice simulation here, I did not feel that I was getting a narrative flow of a story unfolding here but more of a desperate 'do what we can' each turn and hope for the best.  I would not refuse to play it again, nor any other coop game, but it would not be my suggestion.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is a game that everybody should try. It defined the coop niche of board games (although it was not first) by offering a well balanced game where you could choose difficulty level. You really feel like a team trying to solve the world's crises, and thus it is a perfect couple game. There's a lot of table talk going on. The different roles and the randomness of the diseases and epidemics make every game a unique experience. The expansion "On the Brink" makes a perfect game even better. 

Though, it is important to note that the game can suffer from a passive player syndrome. Sometimes you play with people who are not interested in team work or even talking to each other, it's those who'd prefer computer games instead. They can ruin a whole evening because the whole team really need to sync and cooperate to function and succeed with reaching their goals. They will not response when you are trying to discuss your own moves, and when you discuss their moves they will become threatened and defensive. Don't play Pandemic with these people.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Very good co-op game, with the usual strengths and weaknesses but the big advantage that it plays pretty quick.  A very good challenge which rewards further plays - the correct strategies are not obvious and the different combinations of roles really change the game.  Much better when you play with people of roughly the same experience, otherwise the most experienced player will dominate.  It IS good fun!
Update:  more plays now ... Pandemic definitely suffers LESS from the usual co-op problem of one player telling everyone else what to do.  Played a lot of LOTR co-op recently and it suffers much more from this problem, simply because its very important to know what challenges are coming up.  Pandemic is simple and discussions of tactics are pretty inclusive.  Note that it is easy to alter the difficulty level by changing the number of epidemics.
Update again:  you can play this with cards revealed but you are not allowed to talk about tactics unless you are either in the same city OR spend an action (make a phone call).  Works pretty well.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
A really nice co-op game, with a refreshing theme: Save the world from four epidemics. Players move around the board, trying to keep the diseases under control, while also searching for cures.
The players use cards to move about the board quickly. However, the same cards are also used to cure the diseases, creating a really interesting resource managing dilemma.

Cards representing the cities on the board are used to spread the disease. As the cards get cycled back ON TOP of the deck, the epedemics keeps getting worse all the time. Brilliant!
Also, this measn different cities will be hot spots in each game, so there's a lot of replay value.

Players also get five different roles to play for added variety.

Like all co-op games, it's quite hard, constantly handing it to us even on normal difficulty. We are barely able to win on normal difficulty, so I can't immagine how the game is supposed to be beatable on hard difficulty...

Having played some more, especially after adding the first expansion, I've decided to:

Increase the score 8 --> 9!

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
05/30/17 Played a four-player game in 62 minutes. I think Pandemic is fairly well designed, and true to the theme. The components are fine. But the whole game is predicated on the players enjoying the cooperative experience.  I DO NOT!  Hence my low rating.  
   But the worst part to me was, the completely lame role I was given, "the researcher." The experienced players decided who would get which roles. (Hmm, I strongly suspected they should have been doled out randomly. But then I wasn't allowed to see the rule book.)  
   I had no say what so ever. And I was given, in my opinion, the crappiest role in the game. I was basically a doormat. I was told to just lay my cards out face up and the others would just reach over and take whatever cards they wanted. 
   At game end when I complained what a lousy role I'd been given, the experienced players, who had snatched up the "good" roles, just stared at me with a "Yeah, so what, chump? We got what we wanted" look on their faces. I hope to never see Pandemic again (or most of those people).
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I understand why it's already a classic: great theme, easy to learn rules, quick pace, nice components, scalable difficulty, playable with all type of gamers and non gamers...

Still, placing the shuffled Infection Discard pile on top of the remaining Infection Draw is a mechanic that doesn't convince me; I understand it's necessary because othwerise it would be too easy to avoid outbreaks, and it also fastens the pace, but it also creates some non desirable (for me) effects:
-> All the action of the games happens on very specific places; lack of movement through the world
-> Favors the creation of fixed strategies that you'll carry from one game to the next (creation of investigation centers in affected cities to move quickly between spots, etc.). 
-> If 2 epidemy cards are very close one to the other, you'll face a big problem; if this happens twice...

At the end of the day, success on games [for good or for bad] can be determined solely by the [random] placement of the cards.

Still, it's a game I love to play from time to time.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
No of players: solo/2
Co-operative game that sets (right from the beginning) bar really high in this genre.
By using clever mechanisms for changing pace between good, bad and ugly situation on the board, it still gives player filling that nothing is lost until the end.
Instead of just going downhill from one point, it is more like roller coaster all the time. 
More often than not, you'll be in situation to say: "We needed just one more turn, that's all". 
Different roles, event/epidemic/city cards almost ask you to push your luck to the very limit in combination with smart tactic decisions.
Excellent game.
(2015-12-27)
----------------------------------             

For me it is ultimate solo experience. Fantastic game, my personal number 1 and one of the rare games I simply refuse to play cooperatively (it's just a personal preference, for me it feels like a puzzle I want to solve alone). It takes me between 30-45 minutes (with setup) to play full game controlling 3 or 4 characters (with 6 pandemic cards) which is additional plus.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This hasn't produced a boring game yet, though I have only played it a few times.  So far, everyone has liked it.  This is the best co-op I have played (in my limited experience).  I believe it is because no one ever has to "take one for the team".  That has caused tension for us in other co-ops.

I really like the mechanism wherein the infected cities are up for further infections after an epidemic.  This just ups the tension level, which is sustained throughout the game.

I think part of what makes this game work is he wide variation in player powers.  This helps give everyone a stake in what is going on, and a real role to play, since no one else on the team can duplicate the role nearly as effectively.

This was definitely a good purchase.

-------------------------
Update:

I am amazed at how close these games consistently are. Having played this nearly 20 times now, games are nearly always close.  This is just a great game.

See my full review at: 
http://sofrankly.com/2011/04/saving-humankind-from-death-and-disease.html
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Such a good game.  Plays great with just two people, easy enough to play the base game solo (controlling 2 or 3 players yourself).  Good way to introduce people to board games, especially since it's a co-op game and the theme is easily understandable.

What I like best is that you can change the difficultly of the game, and more likely than not the game wins.  Sometimes it opens a can of whup-ass and gives you a double serving!  However it's alway enjoyable win or lose and it feels like the game challenges you to beat it.

Can't say I like the new art on the 2nd edition so I chased down a 1st edition, the map looks so much better and I appreciate havng wooden pieces instead of the new neon plastic ones.  Impossible to get expansions for the 1st edition.  However you can buy the new 2nd edition cards to upgrade the 1st edition directly from z-man games.  If you do this you can use the 2nd edition expansions being released now.

If I could get more people to play the game I would buy the expansions, at least On the Brink.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Although you could find this game rather depressing, you shouldn’t give up just yet.  We must act NOW and we might have a chance to save humanity!
To eradicate this pandemic, we will have to stand together: we need to put in place a strategy to take advantage of our special abilities. Easier said than done… And the clock is ticking.
The game is quite balanced although having the doctor in your team is a significant advantage. The board, cards and pawns are nice.

Certes, au premier abord le contexte du jeu pourrait sembler déprimant... Mais l’heure n’est plus à dépression, il faut agir : êtes-vous capables de sauver l’humanité ? 
Pour venir à bout de cette pandémie à temps, les valeureux joueurs vont devoir faire preuve de solidarité. Mettre en place une stratégie qui tire profit des capacités spéciales de chacun n’est pas si évident, et l’heure tourne… 
Le jeu est assez équilibré mais compter le médecin parmi son équipe donne tout de même un net avantage. Le plateau de jeu, les cartes et les pions sont de bonne qualité.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This game is a classic. Great fully co-operative game that's easy to learn and approachable. It is a puzzle game that gets easier over plays, but allows scaling up difficulty to maintain the challenge. Expect to lose until you get a hang of it - losing as a teamessens the burn somewhat. Having so many ways to lose also keeps things interesting. Randomness is used very well in this game, for initial set up and which cities are affected by epidemic cards. Do have to be careful of alpha gamer factor i.e. the person who has played it the most telling everyone what to do - have to be mindful to let others make their own mistakes, and let them know they can ask advice if needed. What I love about this game is it's as great at 2, 3 or 4. At 2, can always control two characters without any difficulty (4 is a more difficult game as it's harder to get a cure). 

On the Brink is a completely necessary expansion if you enjoy this one. The legacy variants are also well worth delving into once you're familiar with the mechanics.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
After almost a dozen plays, we still have yet to beat it on Introductory level. We have, however, won our first game of Pandemic Legacy. We'll see how that changes going forward. The big lesson learned, from Legacy and playing on the iPad, is that outbreaks seem to be our weakness, and controlling them is more key than I thought it was.

Pandemic is probably the most straight-forward and least complicated co-operative game we own (with the obvious exception of Forbidden Island), making it our game of choice when introducing friends to the co-op genre.

We own the first expansion, but we haven't tried any of the variants contained therein, and I doubt we'll be adding any of the other expansions, for a couple of reasons:

1) We own the 1st edition, so we'd have to buy the compatibility packs; and

2) With Pandemic Legacy out now, regular ol' Pandemic may be about to become obsolete, at least in our house. We'll still keep it, though, for newer players and to combine with the Bio-Terrorist challenge in On The Brink.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
[2010-09-09]
Nagyon jó alaptörténetet találtak ki a játéknak. Vírusok terjednek a Földünkön, amit a csapatban dolgozó orvoscsoport próbál megfékezni az egész bolygón. Repülnek, egymásnak segítenek. Különböző szerepekkel rendelkező játékosok próbálják közösen a játék ellen bevetni minden tudásukat, amire szükség is lesz, mert a játék nehéznek mondható, bár mi az első játékunkat simán nyertük.

A játékidő körülbelül 1 óra, ami akár újbóli vírusirtásra is lehetőséget ad. A játék jól súlyozható, a könnyen megtalálhatja minden csapat a saját izgalmas nehézségi szintjét. Változatos, a kártyák miatt mindig más egy-egy játék.

A három nehézségi szint, a kiegészítővel még tovább növelhető, ezért szerintem nagyon magas az újrajátszhatósági faktora. Méltán van a kooperatív játékok legjobbjai között a Pandemic helye.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Great, simple cooperative game.  Players play agents of the Centre for Disease Control and try to contain 4 different diseases spreading throughout the world.  Each player chooses a different role that has a different special ability.  Players have to travel throughout the world to contain diseases and eventually research cures for them.

This game is quite simple to play and yet quite fun.  It is easy to teach to new players.  I highly recommend this game to introduce new players to board games and/or cooperative games.

The game can be played with 2 to 4 players.  I find that it is easiest with 3 players and hardest with 4 players.  The difficulty level of the game can be adjusted to make it harder for veteran players.

I have the 2013 version.  This fixes some balance issues with one of the roles and adds a new ones.  It also removes one role (the Generalist) which is balanced, but somewhat uninteresting.  Overall, I find that every role is interesting to play and has a unique advantage to help win the game.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Laura's Rank (3/15) – 5 out of 5. Pros: I like cooperative games overall. The theme is played out so well that even competitive people will get drawn into beating the board. I love that you can control the difficulty with the epidemic cards. You can play it over and over and have it still be interesting and challenging. I love the components and how it looks when you are overwhelmed with diseases. Great player interaction. You have to work together as a team, which is not necessarily true of all cooperative games. So many ways to die. Just a great game. Complicated enough to think through strategies, but not so complicated that you can't have fun the first time you play.

Ryan's Rank (3/15) – 5 out of 5. This is a great game. Easily my favorite cooperative. Love the theme. Love the mechanics. Love that you really have to work as a team to beat the game. There are some tense moments that come in the game, and Laura and I tend to get into it. Our friends have also taken to it as well.

Overall Rank: 10 out of 10
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: this is an okay game ... try to stamp out diseases before they over-run the planet, this is strictly a co-operative game, and thereby can be a danger -- the danger is this game plays via committee -- and I hate committees (having had enough of them in real life) ... the strongest tends to take over, and if you are easy-going, you find your moves, are not really 'your moves' .. go here; do this; no, no, WE think you should be over here; -- and so you go for the betterment of the species -- game can be challenging though, as disease spreads faster than the group can stamp it out; so this is good -- but your unique character becomes subsumed to the will of 'the committee' ... and you just knew your own move was the right one after all -- can be fun with the right group, but painful if not the right group -- seeing as co-op games are not my favs -- let me go and make my mistakes (and my total hate of all committees) .. although I would play this if tabled -- tis far from my first choice -- but it is an okay game
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
First play with 2 players on easy was fun, but we were close to winning. Started over to add third player (normal) and that ramped up the fun and tension considerably. We lost the game within 40 minutes! Can't wait to try again. Never played a co-op game before and this genre hits a sweet spot that is sorely missing from my games and all games in general. I hope designers pick up on this mechanic and run with it!

Update: Our second 3 player game was so tense, such a nailbiter to the end, that I got a stomache ache. I love it! We had one round (six card draws) to figure out a way for one person to give another person the needed cards to cure the fourth and final disease. We threw strategies back and forth, and at one point seemed so close to a solution, but to no avail. The last infection draw of the game caused the final outbreak, and we lost even before we could try for a cure. This game now goes up to a 9, my first 9, based on the excitement of that 3 player game. 

Update: game quickly lost its appeal.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Brilliant design. This is a game that truly meets the criteria "for non-gamers and gamers alike". Great two player or solo game as well. Very compact box, easy to travel with and sets up pretty fast. 

The real crux of the game, and why it is rated so highly by most, is the card driven mechanic that ramps up the intensity in a perfectly escalating trend of greater and greater alarm and sheer panic. Can be very intense and fun the whole way through. 

One criticism: the player pawns are way too big for the map. We use miniature figures instead of the pawns now anyway, so no biggie. Yes, i know the expansion fixes this.  

Note - changed rating from 9 to 8. Problem is that because of the luck of the cards, there are times when you just simply can not win. On the other hand, there are times that you win rather easily because the cards just came out that way. Still a wonderful game and an easy 8, but had to drop my respect slightly because this aspect of the game tends to frustrate one the more you play.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: The game plays very quickly. There is a lot of table talk and this can cause some players to have their turns practically played out for them. As long as it is a group discussion and everyone agrees on the plan of action I don't see this as a problem. Much of the fun of the game was running through different scenarios which would play out several turns in advance to beat the game. But then the game throws a curve ball and it's back to the drawing board. We played 2 beginner setup games and lost the first one (minus the researcher) and won the second (minus the medic). I'm looking forward to playing with the standard setup next. 4 more beginner games (1-3). We won the one without the operations expert. *UPDATE* 5/13. My friend (dispatcher) and I (Op.Spec.) beat Heroic level. It helped that we didn't pull any black cities in the initial 9 and that area was the first to be cured and sunshined. *UPDATE* 5/20 BEat heroic level again. This time with scientist and medic. We sunshined Blue and Red fairly quickly.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Wonderful game - great sense of escalation.  It is always a climactic ending for us - whether we win or lose. We can usually find the first cure quickly, and things can be quiet until you find the second one.  But if you feel you've had a break early in the game, things will ramp up pretty quickly after the second cure is found.  Even when  things are quiet, there is tension because you know something big is coming. This is a sign of great design.  This is my opinion after about 25 plays. I feared that it would get stale as a 2-player game, but I am happy to say it hasn't been so.  We regularly play on level 6 with the base game and level 5 with On the Brink.  It is also great with more players.  A little more difficult, as you each have fewer turns and need to coordinate very well. But you have to play with the right group:  don't play it with alpha-gamers or people who are sensitive about others offering suggestions.  It will mar your experience with this game if you play a game like that early on.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
The prototypical cooperative game. Different roles work together to cure all the diseases in the world. The plays are basically playing against the board and racing against the clock to get diseases cured by running around the board removing cubes from cities and building research stations to eventually find a cure, etc. The game can definitely snowball on you as you draw more and more bad cards. 

I think this game is best played where you can't share information from your hand with other players. Like Shadows over Camelot you have to speak vaguely. Otherwise you'll get prone to planning moves way ahead of time and getting analysis paralysis. The worst problem is definitely quarterbacking though. If you have played it before and others haven't, make sure you really tone back the telling people what to do. It's helpful to give hints, but not to straight up plan peoples moves.

I like this game. It's definitely quality. But it's not my favorite, or even my favorite coop. I'd recommend playing it though.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: This game has been a treasure to bust out and play every time without fail. When I was in the military and morale was low, I’d host game nights with my work buddies and Pandemic was a top favorite! Eventually I bought the entire Legacy series but I haven’t started playing them until recently (currently just starting the first game in Season 1). I didn’t have a reliable enough group of people to commit to the campaign plus we were all busy. All that’s changed now. I also enjoy teaching others how to play it. It’s pretty simple to learn yet tricky to master. I’ve since added several Pandemic and Pandemic System games to my collection! Pandemic is the game I use to hook others into the world of board gaming! I have no criticisms of it at all. I know many say it’s prone to “quarterbacking” or “alpha gaming” but that would be an issue with any cooperative game. Thats a player issue. Not a game issue. Easily my favorite board game ever and an immediate go to for me! Highly recommend to anyone and everyone!!!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Interesting.  I can see this being much more replayable than other cooperative games, what with the way the roles and the infected cities come into play.  I can also see it falling prey to the "Meathead" effect, where the most experienced player dominates the decisions made by the group, but I think it's less pronounced than with other games in this category.  I think it's important for ANY cooperative game to allow players to discover it on their own.  A good leader can direct play without being pushy.

It took a while to begin playing the game correctly, but even during that time, it had a lot of appeal to it, and it has that "tickle" effect, where it settles in the brain for further analysis.  It's not a deep game, by any means, but I can see it being enjoyable, and easy to teach.  And because of the trickiness to remembering the rules, be aware that if your first game seems too easy, you're likely playing it incorrectly.

4 plays: 1 player

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
My first expeience with a co-op game apart from Lord of the Rings, and I really enjoyed it. Rating is based on a single play and first impression. The game utilizes some very innovative mechanics, not the least of which is when the diseases "intensify" by reshuffling the discard deck and placing them back on top of the draw pile. This is an excellent and clever mechanic that had us scratching our heads at first, until the lightbulb of understanding shone upon us...

UPDATE: I've now played this lots of times, and my rating stands.  It is tense and enjoyable, even if fairly random. The intial placement of 3-cube diseases relative to the players' starting position in Atlanta can have a huge impact, as can the randomly selected player roles, when the first Epedemic card turns up, and when the special cards turn up (if they are near the bottom of the deck, they're not going to be of much help). Despite the random aspects, I still really enjoy it. I think it's one of the most innovative games in years.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is a co-op game that is not that hard to teach to non-gamers. This is the kind of game you want to play again and again until you beat it together. If you finally do that it feels really rewarding. But it is not an easy game. There are different levels of the game, but even the easy mode is hard enough the first couple of games.  

The game is both thematic and engaging. Every one of your actions can be crucial for the entire group. So you have to be careful and think through what to do. I've heard some complaints that this makes the game suffer from the alphaplayer problem, which is that one experienced or leader-oriented player are making all the decisions. I have not found this to be much of a problem in my different gaming groups I've played it with though.

This is a wonderfully designed game that I almost always enjoy playing. The mechanics are so connected and the game is well balanced. If I would have to pick one co-op game to keep in my collection, this would be the one.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is a fun cooperative game, ironically similar to our real lives right now, where you are trying to cure and eradicate some diseases across the globe. You use your turn for 4 actions that can include moving, transportation, curing a disease, treat a disease at that location, using a character's ability, or building a a research facility. You can cure a disease at a research facility by having 5 cards of that disease's color, then if you want to eradicate the disease to prevent it from spawning through the infection deck, you have to treat all of the locations that it is currently at. 

Pandemic is a fun game that is probably much more realistic than people probably originally thought it was going to be when they first picked it up. It's a fairly quick game, but much harder when you don't have the researcher on your team. I would definitely recommend it because it's a fun cooperative game and there are already way more good competitive board games than there are cooperative ones.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
+ On the Brink expansion
+ In the Lab expansion

Rating based on SOLO play only.

It's like solving a big puzzle whose parameters keep changing and evolving. Great sense of rising tension and good frustration (there's always a feeling of "if I only had ONE more action..."). I find the game design very elegant in how the virus spreads and how quickly the game can change, yet it does so in a very organic way.

Expansion comments: 
-On the Brink: I tend to not use the Mutation and Virulent Strain modes very often because I think the base game is hard enough for me, but the extra role/event cards and the petri dishes (a nice thematic touch) make this a good expansion to have 
-In the Lab: really changes things up and after just a couple of plays I don't think I'd play without this now


---------------------------

Sold. A great game, but since I didn't play very often and didn't need the huge amount of variety, I think Pandemic Iberia will cover me nicely with a smaller amount of space.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
A lovely co-op that's at the right level of complexity to feel like a challenge, while still being accessible and enjoyable to those who are new to games.

It's like the first boss of a video game.  There are so many better games out there than Pandemic, but conquering it can open a newbie's eyes to what modern boardgames can truly offer, and give them the conceptual toolbox to go out and conquer bigger prey.

On its own, Pandemic isn't much of a game.  You struggle against a random card draw that evolves into a repetitive AI to cleanse the world of cubes.  
The chaos of the cards - and thus the AI - means that winning will oscillate between punishingly difficult and mindlessly easy, and the effort you put into the game won't necessarily translate into meaningful outcomes.

That Said, Pandemic does a good job instilling a sense of teamwork and camaraderie in the face of an implacable enemy, and it feels good when you see your unified struggle start to pay off if you make progress.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This was the first super successful co-op game on the market, although Lord of the Rings pre-dates it and would have done ok too.

Players must work together and make use of the abilities that their role offers them in order to save the world from a series of infectious diseases. 

The game works brilliantly on two levels. Diseases have the ability to spread and break out based on where they occur on the board and the deck of cards is constructed in such a way that locations that have seen the disease will appear again within a given timeframe, which can then lead to outbreaks.

It all adds up to an experience where the players know the clock is ticking but they aren't quite sure when the timebomb will go off. They then have to make the right choices to juggle the multiple threats and they only have limited resources with which to to do. 

Brilliant although can be dominated by an experienced player - so get the playing group right and ensure that decisions are made by the group.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: 8 - I was really suprised by this game, I tried the Matt Leacock co-op trilogy at PAX and walked away with Pandeminc AND Forbidden Island.  Pandemic grabs me the best, it's a solid theme that's simultaneously serious and lighthearted.  Most games I play I find myself running short on time because of the player deck, with 4 players you end up with ~12 turns each time flies by quickly and all of a sudden you realize you won't get another turn after this one and the viruses overrun everything.  I find it a challenge and actually enjoy this with 2~3 people way more than 4~5 but still try to play it with new people whenever I can.  It's a nice gateway game because it breaks several molds at once; it is totally cooperative, it has a fixed turn count thanks to the player deck, it's fairly randomized without any dice, and it has a good amount of strategy "we don't need to worry about mexico since it just came up and we had an epidemic last turn, so lets focus on europe a little more."
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Interesting mechanic for a game, but difficult to find the right group of players (without a strong alpha).  In my family, everyone has an opinion and everyone wants to approach the situation their way.  I don't get to game that much, but when I do, I want to be able to select a strategy without having to settle for an inferior one or having to fight to defend a better one (so I guess I fit right in).

It is also difficult to find just the right difficulty level - it seems that the game is either too easy to beat or impossible to beat (with On the Brink).  There aren't enough games in the middle where different play would have made the difference between winning and losing.  After the game ends, I never find myself saying, if I only moved to Rio...  

Rating for first few plays: 7.5, Rating for subsequent plays 6 (once the uniqueness of cooperative play and having the recently used infection cards return to the top of the deck wore off for me).  But, my family still enjoys it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Ok.  I've got 8 plays under my belt so I feel it is safe to comment on this game.  I would say the best way to describe this is that the win-loss seems to be like solitaire -- you don't necessarily know if you are going to win when you begin, but it certainly feels like it is pre-ordained before you even begin.  It's through playing the game that you even know if you stand a chance.  Further, the game really seems to lend itself to players that are power control freaks.  Rather than each player trying their best, it seems that one person needs to dictate specific strategies to get anywhere -- and the likelihood of you winning can be nil if the (bad) luck of the draw screws you over.  Not fun.  We've won 1 game out of 8.  If you like to lose and move your pieces at someone elses behest, then this game is for you.  Otherwise, I recommend moving along.

UPDATE:  Wahooo!!  I traded this game off to someone.  Thank goodness for BGG! :)  I'm now the lucky owner of a Mah Jong set.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Update:  This has been a great 2 player game for me, many, many, plays. It's easy to misplay a rule or two and get an incorrect impression of the game.  Repeated plays have earned this game a 9, and with the extra roles in the expansion I consider it a 10.



Really a great game to introduce friends to boardgaming.  Short and tense!  The theme is great and makes you feel like a character from a Michael Crichton novel trying to save mankind from diseases.  It's a game you can have the folks from up the street try out without having them be an elf or an orc- the scientific theme is refreshing.  I hope the success of this game gets us more short cooperative games.  As a gamer I prefer Lord of the Rings as a cooperative because it feels bigger and has more decisions as well as more options as you play.  Pandemic is so short and lean that how the deck is stacked might determine the game before it starts.  Enjoyable and easy, I need to play more to see if it gets better for me.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I played it once and immediately bought my own copy and have played that more than one hundred times since, and I will still try to start games. The co-operative aspect is great: it has brought in players who are otherwise turned off by the competitiveness of boardgaming. The rules don't take too long to explain to a newcomer. The motif is brilliant for the mechanic, and fun and interesting. The play is interesting and the difficulty level can be adjusted to suit your game. The 5 different roles* make the game more interesting.

It is not without it's faults (although I don't consider any of these faults): particularly that the randomness of the card deck means that sometimes the game is much harder or a bit easier. It seems particularly well-suited to 3 player, although 2 and 4 are both fine (and I play more often in 2 or 4). There's no winner.


*Or 6: it's beneficial and easy to add the Generalist Role from the expansion (it just gives 5 actions per turn).
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: I just picked this up today(2/22) from my FLGS and I'm glad I ventured out to get it!  Initial rating based on solitaire play.  This game is very cool and very tense.  For me, tension is one of those high qualities in a game and this one works well, even if you're all alone! :)  I'm curious to see how it will play with others but, unlike other card games, this one does seem to work well solitaire.  My game ended with the red cubes exhausted and all I needed was one turn to get the scientist to Tokyo, do the cure with his four cards and boom, there was still a chance!  But alas, it was not meant to be! :cry:  Somehow, I think I'll be playing this one quite a bit over the weekend!Update:  I finally won! :D  However, it was on the intro. setting and I had only three cards left in the deck, the next one being the fourth epidemic! :gulp: :what:  After 14 plays, I am a dismal 3-11, :shake:  but that is part of the appeal of this game: the challenge of beating the system!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is indeed a very enjoyable co-op game.  Not to mention it is very solid as a solitaire game.  It is, as advertised on BGG, very difficult to win.  However, it can be done so it doesn't get to the point where it's frustrating.  I have only played a small hand full of times so far, so my current rating may fluctuate some after a few more plays.

I do need to mention the components.  Either the board is too small, or the pieces are too big..maybe a little of both.  Either way, the board can get awfully cluttered when an area gets busy.  Often times you will not even be able to see the names of the cities underneath all the cubes, pawns, and research stations.  This forces you to move things around on the board and it is very easy to get cubes of the same color pushed around, thus making it easy to possibly end up with a cube on a city it shouldn't be on.  I suppose after many plays you will memorize the city locations, but at least initially it is quite annoying.

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is an exceptionally well crafted game. Just sitting back and watching the game system work is part of the joy of playing. The masterstroke is the way the discard pile gets shuffled and stacked on top of the deck at somewhat unpredictable intervals. That simple rule generates an amazing amount of paranoia.

With experienced players, I recommend playing with 5 epidemic cards and the infection rate boosted to start on the second space. Other ideas for increasing difficulty include (1) removing some cubes from one or two diseases, (2) requiring the eradication of one of the diseases (either a specific one or a freely-chosen one), or (3) adding the 6th epidemic card. Smaller player counts tend to make for easier games, so it's nice to have an arsenal of tweaks that can be added or subtracted.

If you want to play solo, you can of course simulate any number of players, but you can also try playing with just one character (preferably the Scientist or the Medic).
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Well, I had this at an 8 for some time, but I HAVE to bump it to a 9 now, for the very reason that every single person I have introduced it to absolutely loves it. Whereas losing always has everyone excited and emotional. Maybe my friends are just weird. I'm  also not so sure about the re-playability, it's starting to feel a bit tired even after 7 plays. Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
[b]A potentially great game where the immersion is ruined by character selection issues due to a lack of all male characters and no way to choose your character.[/b]

Pros:
* Great theme and production quality.
* Great board that gives the game a nice tactical layout.
* Variable roles with different abilities makes you feel like an actual team trying to fight a pandemic.

Cons:
* [b]-1 for potentially being forced to play as a female character.[/b]
* -1 for not having any choice of your character at the start of the game.
* Forced limited rounds by running out of player cards is lame.
* Petri dishes should have been included with the original game to store the virus tokens.
* Without any expansions the game gets very repetitive, [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgameexpansion/40849/pandemic-brink]On The Brink[/url] is an essential expansion.

I only recommend getting the latest edition (2012) as the component quality is phenomenally better than the original.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
It has some cool mechanisms but in my opinion it got published while still in design stage. Some tweakings needed.

After having played it a bit you realize that, no matter how efficiently you play, winning/losing actually depends way too much on the randomness of the travelling/curing deck and how it distributes color cards among the players during the match. Get a heavenly shuffle and you'll likely win. Get an evil shuffle though and you'll likely bite the dust no matter what.

With some simple home rules you may make up for these lacking design issues (like increase hand limit to 8, don't count event cards for hand limit, allow the reshuffle of the traveling/curing discard pile to form a new deck if the previous is depleted, loosen restrictions to cards sharing... In other words: finish the work the game designer left undone).

Something around 35€ taking an hour to play shouldn't behave like a 'flip-a-coin-find-the-winner', and Pandemic does, quite a bit.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Playing team solitaire is the most uninteresting game imaginable. Winning team solitaire is the most unsatisfying win there is

In  my opinion co-ops are the worst games made. Pandemic does not stand out in any way in this genre. It’s probably a decent game for children with overprotective parents who shrink at the notion of competition. It’s probably a decent game for social gamers. 

I note that Pandemic has been available at Walmart for a couple years. Perhaps it may serve as a gateway game for people, I just pray that they progress to good games before they get tired of this nonsense.

If games are designed for teams, there should be an opposing team. Without opposition there is no game. You can lose a game against a team and you can be satisfied that you played well, or draw inspiration to play better next time. Pandemic is the boardgame equivalent of playing computer poker for no money against a poorly programmed bot that never varies its style of play.

textfield_comment_value:
1st game...well we decided to play the 'easy' route and owner of game set it up and we ran through it.  We won.  I'm usually not happy about a co-op game that can be beaten in the first play when you don't know the system well and probably are making some extra moves that don't need to be made. Well as it turns out we seeded the deck wrong...and actually had an "Ultra-easy" game on our hands as we played without 2 epidemic cards.  

Now for the game play. I love it.  You feel a real sense of urgency in this game it feels so important to get so much done in such a little amount of time.  This can be a brutal game if we'd have had even one of the extra epidemics in there I think we'd have lost.  Fun game very intense. 

I do feel this is one of those "expansions in mind" games and won't be surprised if we see an expansion for it sooner rather than later.
