Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I've played this game a few times now and I personally enjoy the co-op gameplay much better because it makes for a much more enjoyable gaming experience when playing casually (my wife and I are both very competitive so it's nice to break from that). The theme elements are cool and the game components are pretty high quality. I especially enjoy playing with 4 players because the action is much better when you have a larger group. I will say that the game setup can be a little tedious; the disease cubes are numerous and you have to be really careful not to bump the board or you'll end up infecting all of Europe.

Pros: Great strategic co-operative gameplay. Quality game components. Lots of replay value and a nice difficulty scaling system.

Cons: So many little bits to keep track of. Disease cubes are cumbersome sometimes to deal with.

Bottom line: One of the best games I own. Certainly worth the purchase and I would even consider the expansion packs.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
(RUS) Пандемия (Pandemic) - #99 место на бгг

О чём игра: Чистый кооператив, в котором мы перемещаемся по карте мира и пытаемся вылечить 4 эпидемии.

Тесто: Глобально игра задаёт 2 вопроса: как выиграть и как не проиграть. Чтобы победить, нужно собрать на руке 5 карточек одного цвета. Чтобы не проиграть, нужно бегать по всему миру и лечить болезни, на что тоже тратятся эти же самые карточки. Математически, всё сводится к балансу между "копить для победы" и "тратить для избежания проигрыша".

Изюм: Для меня эта игра - такая лёгкая головоломка с элементами случайности. Уникальная специальность для каждого игрока даёт ощущение собственной значимости. Самый большой плюс этой игры для меня - то, что в неё можно играть вообще в любой компании, независимо от опыта игроков. Отлично подходит для первой настолки в жанре кооперативов.

Оценка: 6 из 10, хорошая игра, с удовольствием поиграю, если не хочется особо напрягаться и конкурировать с другими игроками.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Cuatro enfermedades se han desatado en el mundo y encontrar la cura depende de un equipo de especialistas en distintos campos.
Los jugadores deben trabajar juntos aprovechando al maximo las habilidades de sus personajes y planificando estrategias para erradicar definitivamente las enfermedades antes de que acaben con el planeta.

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Pandemic - introduces co-op and some really clever mechanics not to mention its fantastic looking! So if you are looking for a game that showcases modern board gaming, this is a very good example. It has a very low entry point as most players don't need to know what they're doing at all. And role cards and random disease locations will create some variety for repeat plays. It's main problem as a gateway game is you need to be extremely deliberate about keeping new players involved in each decision or you risk them becoming passengers and not gaining a sense of achievement or ownership. Another issue is that on the one hand you have a risk of the whole group losing, which may not be very satisfying. And of course you could just set the difficulty really low, but then you might give the feeling of there not being much of a challenge. Will best suit group of similar experience or at least people who are equally confident sharing their opinion.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
An extremely clever but curiously soulless cooperative game. The mechanic through which infected cities get recycled back on top of the deck is simple but outstanding; it creates a compelling narrative arc and ratchets up the tension pleasantly in tune with the course of the game. The differing roles help differentiate  options and the constant board changes between turns ensure constant tactical reappraisals and adjustments. And at short and breezy, the length is right too.

On the other hand, mechanically the game is also very much a dry mathematical optimization exercise, with little thematic heft or draw. Nothing within is evocative of any research enterprise, medical field work, or disease epidemic, which robs some appeal from the design. Still, it really is one of the best cooperative games out there, if you play at a reasonable pace and can get past the fact, like all such games, opportunities for true individual decisions are rare.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: The shuffling mechanic which causes certain cities to reinfect repeatedly (and gives you information about where the diseases will be coming from) is brilliant.I like the short length, which is much better for a cooperative game.  I also like how this game is not about just learning the strategy of what you need to do (how you need to spend your resources), and then having the person who knows the correct strategy dictate to the others what to do.  Rather, its actually a complicated tactical puzzle, one that actually benefits from having more than one brain thinking about it, and discussing it.  This game made me realize that cooperative games need to be promarily tactical, not strategic in nature, and need to be tactically difficult enough that anyone is going to need help from their partners in figuring it out, thus leading to true cooperation, not just the experienced player dictating moves to the rest (like in Shadows and in LotR).

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Play this game with your friends, your family, or any group and you'll find out personality types right quick.  There are those who plan out the next round of moves for the group and those who end up just moving the pieces.

And that's the blessing and the curse of this game.  The cooperative game play is a lot of fun, but when you have a team goal and a team approach, the individuals playing don't really matter as much which can turn some people off the game pretty early on.

My wife, my mother, my sister, and I have strong personalities and don't have problems making ourselves heard.  And we all like games of one type or another.  But my sister and I started talking strategy and my mother and wife were looking at their phones.  Is that a reflection on my sister and I?  Probably.  But it's also a dynamic that this game can easily encourage.

I'd absolutely play it whenever anyone suggested.  But maybe with a different group next time.

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is part of my 'gateway' collection, used to introduce family and friends to modern boardgames.
THE benchmark in co-operative games and an ideal introduction to the co-op genre.
The simple premise that ALL players are a team against the game itself often provides such a different experience of gaming that people are energised when they first play and can't wait to play again.
Themeing is spot on (if a little close to the bone in these COVID days), gameplay is easy enough to pick up, though is greatly assisted if someone has played before, and the dynamic nature of the puzzle provides a great group-think challenge.
The variety of roles and the random nature of the deck provide ample replayability. It's a sense of team achievement to win when playing at the 'normal' level, its proper elation if you succeed against the 'hardest' difficulty!
Just need to be careful that one player doesn't take over and that all of the team have input.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
A quick and easy game to understand, and a very family-friendly game, that almost anyone in the household can participate in.

The game itself is quite entertaining, as long as you get the right combination of roles. We had a lengthy discussion about whether the roles were imbalanced, which was due to some characters being less useful than others. The doctor is amazing, as well as the scientist guy, whereas the coordinator and the quarantine guy, whom is very specialized. In the end, we reckoned that a way to get around this, if it is an issue, would be to acquire the roles, and then adjust the difficulty. In that way, you make sure that if you get a bad combination or a very good combination, that the game is adjusted for that. 

This is normally only needed if you have a group that is used to playing board games, whereas playing with the family, it might just be hilarious to loose, which is kind of the point of this game I guess.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Honestly Pandemic isn't really my cup of tea. I decided to go ahead and buy it after a few years of looking at such high reviews. The first time I played this game in a group of 3 it was not bad. Towards the end it was getting a little crazy but it was all calmed down in the end. The second time I played it in a group of 4 and that time around I decided to make the difficulty harder since there was an extra person. Yet that turned into the easiest game I have ever played in my life. We all just kind of took our turns without a care in the world. The outbreaks never got anywhere near out of hand, each virus was controlled, and we found a cure for them all without any stress inhibiting situations. We won the game yet there was no satisfaction for winning. We all just sat around the board asking, "That's it?" Maybe I'll give the game another chance sometime later down the line but for now it will definitely not be one of my go to games.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic was my first co-op game experience, and it is still one of my favorite all-time games. While it's notoriously difficult to win (I've only won about 1/3 of the games I've played), it's not impossible. Although it's a lot of fun, though, Pandemic is not without its flaws. The two big caveats I would give it are:

- Winning is actually not that much fun. The times I've had the most fun with Pandemic are when my group loses and we instantly want to play another round. This never happens when we win.
- If you're playing with people who are *too* focused on winning and not as focused on letting people make difficult decisions, it can turn into a situation where one player is just telling everyone else what to do, which can be pretty annoying.

Regardless, Pandemic is one of those games I'm ALWAYS down to play, which is saying something. It's easy to teach to new people, but the randomness of events makes it incredibly replayable.
Title: Pandemic

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: My personal favorite co-operative game, Pandemic has you playing the role of one of five distinct international medical specialist, whose job is to work with between one and three other specialists to find the cures for four deadly and infectious diseases before they overrun the planet.  This game has just the right mixture of simplicity, co-operation, variety, and tension that gives it near infinite replayability.  While a pretty simple game to get the hang of, it is still incredibly difficult to win at times, and the mounting tension in some games can be pretty intense, so the game can certainly be intimidating.  That said, this is one game I keep coming back to, and provided you play with people who like to work together with others towards a common good, you will love this game.  The apocalyptic biological plague theme, while not laid thick, works very well with mechanics.  Highly recommended, as is the wonderful expansion.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Even though the game is made for up to 4 players, it can still be played by 5 players. You just have to deal 1 card in the beginning for every player. Yes, it does lower the success chance of the game, but it can be done.

You just really have to focus on finding the vaccines fast and talk/communicate a lot with other players about the steps your group needs to make as a whole while not letting infection spread pile up.

As the cooperation is a really big part in this game and you want everyone to have a good time, it is one of the first games I recommend to others. You can get the fulfilling moments when clearing the game only just in the nick of time; or when your group suffer defeat, because you guys almost made it, but it was so exhilarating and even in defeat you get memorable experience and likely talk with the group what to try the next time, even though you know that each game is not going to be the same as the last.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is simple and quick, suitable for all audiences sort of game in the co-operative "stuff happens on the board and you deal with it" genre. Not much detail, not much chrome, easy to get into, with some of this semi-limited information to address issues of coop games. It works as a non-offensive lowest common denominator, because it is fairly simple, doesn't ask for much investment and features many of the characteristics which are widely popular. 

In co-operative games, there is a line between playing as a team and telling everybody what to do in their turn. Pandemic is very prone to that issue, because playing the game feels like solving a more or less trivial puzzle. And when gameplay is primarily about finding the optimal choice, there will naturally be one person simply stating the obvious.

I recognize that this is a well designed and foundational game, but I'm not very much interested in what it has to offer.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
What is there to say about Pandemic that has not already been said?

I love this game, I really do, however, it can feel a little redundant after a couple of plays, and as with most co-op games, you always run the risk of having an alpha player take over.

My biggest complaint is that sometimes you can feel like you never really have a TURN, even if there is no alpha player. Everyone is just always involved at all times, which is part of the fun, and partly what attracted me to the game and what I love about it, but a side effect of that is that you never really feel like you are playing your turn. There's no sense of personal ownership, if that makes sense.

I'm looking forward to playing with some of the expansions, and especially the Legacy games, to see how they change up gameplay. This is a GREAT introduction to cooperative games, and it was actually my first foray into the hobby outside of Monopoly and Risk. Love it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is an engaging game with a theme that draws you in right from the start. I particularly enjoy the thematic elements, although I wish the cubes represented the sickness more effectively. The game's difficulty adjustments are well-designed, allowing for varied levels of challenge. I was pleasantly surprised by the fan-made solo mode, which turned out to be very enjoyable. The rulebook is clear and easy to understand, making the game accessible to new players.

However, some of the player roles aren't as enjoyable. For instance, drawing the Contingency Planner, even with the Dispatcher, can make the game less fun for us, as we prefer not to cheat. Despite not being a huge fan of cooperative games, Pandemic has become one of the gateway games that got me into the board gaming hobby. I believe it can become even more enjoyable with expansions. I can see myself playing Pandemic every now and then, even after 5-10 years.
Title: Pandemic

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Initially, I loved Pandemic. It was a simple, elegant design, that could be played by any and all with a theme that didn't turn off anyone. The fact that the game also played quickly gave it a chance to hit the table quicker - something to do in between events instead of waiting specifically for a "Game Night".

That said, each game leaves me slightly wanting more. I'm not begging for a traitor (I'm in the minority of actually not caring much for that mechanic); but it feels so rote - so demanding that the role you choose must be played in a particular fashion or everyone suffers.

Occassionally, I can still rise to the challenge. I want to be the (insert role here) and see if I can take on six epidemics; but with so many other games out there...as much fun as others have putting this on the table, I'd like to play something new.

Until something like Swine Flu twists me up...then it's a Pandemic Weekend Jamboree!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:

For the moment I must say that my enjoyment is really varied for this game. I like it when there is difficulty but depending on the number of epidemics, it could be a very easy and thus boring game.

[u]March 2010:[/u] So, in a sense, Pandemic was a good buy as it convinced me to try a little more Co-op games. I later bought Ghost Stories and boy is ghost stories a lot funnier and challenging! Yeah luck is more contained and this should be a big advantage in my book, but here, it just makes the game a bit too easy. It is nice to play but it doesn't really challenge us.

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I ADORE this game. To me, this game is the king of anxiety-inducing, tense, edge-of-your-seat experiences. The co-op nature truly builds comraderie, and each person feels useful and helpful in averting Armageddon.

The art is excellent, and the bits are all well-constructed and designed. The pace of the game is amazingly fine-tuned, and you'll always feel one step away from defeat. This is a GOOD thing, as the game is intended to simulate a world-ending outbreak of diseases. If you didn't feel constantly under pressure, the theme wouldn't shine.

I highly recommend getting the On The Brink expansion. The vanilla game is awesome, but once you add in the fifth disease, new event/epidemic cards, and the option to have a player be a Bio-Terrorist and play AGAINST the rest of the group, Pandemic really takes off.

This game is a go-to game for my family, and I think anyone who is intrigued by the premise will love it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Great theme and design for a co-op, although I'm almost disappointed that our group won our first game. I suspect that this game becomes less interesting the better you get at it, which is the opposite of what I typically look for. Still, for what it is, and with the right group, Pandemic is fun. I'd be happy to play again in similar circumstances. But I don't see myself requesting it over a good competitive game.

After another play with a different group and another win, I feel the same as I did after my first play. I guess I should be playing it at the highest level of difficulty. Even so, I'm not sure how I feel about co-ops like Pandemic. You play against the system; you try to be as efficient as you can; and you hope that the cards don't kill you. True, there's some excitement in that, but it's sobering to look at the game from an analytical point of view and realize that ultimately your choices may not matter.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This co-op game is nice in that it allows the players to control the difficulty.  If you're playing with a group of new players you may choose to use the minimum number of epedimic cards in the infection deck.  If you are playing with a group of experienced Pandemic players who want a real challenge then load up the infection deck with all of the epedimic cards...just don't expect to win.  Great fun for all, with multiple roles to choose from offering good replayability.

textfield_comment_value:
An absolute classic. I have a feeling that I may have felt this way about whatever my first board-based “putting out fires” co-op was, but it’s hard to play any others without just thinking I’d rather play Pandemic. It’s a genre where all of the games feel pretty similar to me. Regardless, Pandemic was the one I learned first and played many many times (probably 100+, before I tracked plays), and went deep on strategy and analysis. It holds up to extremely deep analysis, and every move of every game is important, so I think it’s an easy recommendation for someone looking for a deep co-op. 

The On the Brink expansion adds a lot!  The base game is pretty easy to win ~80% of games with enough skill, and having the mutation and virulent strain really makes it difficult. Too difficult to win consistently, but every small incremental increase in player skill significantly improves your chances, making it very rewarding.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: It's good that the difficulty is selectable in this game.  They seemed to have done a good job balancing it.   The tension is excellent, but I think the game will get repetitive quickly.   It also suffers from that fact that it is more of a multiplayer puzzle than a game.  Everybody agrees what should be done, and there is very little opportunity for style or choice.  It's kind of like getting your friends together to change the head gasket on your car.  There's some similarity to Shadows Over Camelot if you look under the hood - move around and collect sets of cards.   That's it.  The movement is a little more important here than Shadows. Still, it's nice to have a fresh co-op style game, but I don't think this game will have any staying power after you have a few wins under your belt.  I suppose expansions will address that needed variability.   Co-ops aren't my cup of tea, so my rating here is on the low side.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Several games played with most of the games being close wins or losses. Upped the rating from 7 to 8 as it is socially enjoyable with 2. Probably the best introduction to the attitude shift involved in co-operative games, better than say Scotland Yard in that:- a)the short playing time allows a repeat to improve and consolidate performance; b)the problem of 1 player wanting to dominate the proceedings is tempered by what the held cards allow, which encourages everyone to socialize; c)more tense countdown elements and one use only cards to consider. One thing that comes to mind is that I complained about 2 chaotic subsystems in La Citta recently, and here they are again, but I can tolerate the card draws as amongst the team we can "discuss" a workable route through the chaos. Update: I was alittle concerned about replay value, but after a dozen plays it is still a fun, tense and quick experience, so up the rating.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
If I were a virus, I would make sure to show basically no symptoms in the first weeks. This way, nobody would notice  I'm even there, and all your logistics experts would sleep happily in their beds and dream of their ugly girlfriends, not giving a damn about planning new CDC research centers. 

If I were a virus, I would show an evolutionary preference for certain climatic conditions (officially, I don't even qualify as life form, so don't you dare call me a racist). This way, your quarantine specialist wouldn't even know where to start when I suddenly pop up at all the end-of-the-world-places that take him so much time to travel to. 

If I were a virus, I would mutate a lot. This way, your scientist lady at the WHO would need so many more samples of me before having the slightest clue how I even look like. 

If I were I virus, I'd get you all.

Pandemic teaches as lot about viruses. How lucky I am not a virus.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is probably my favourite game in my collection. It may not be the one I personally like best (that's Agricola currently), but it's the one that the most people enjoy that we get to play most often. It has an excellent balance of complexity, tactics, and fun that lets a new player pick up the game quickly and old players settle in and have fun each time. The expansions add a ton of depth and variation to play. And it's fun to play even with just me and my wife, which is an unusual feature in a game.

NOTE: The best rule we ever implemented was a limited amount of table-talk. This is a game where some players tend to boss around other players. When we're playing with one of those people, we use an egg-timer at the start of each turn. That timer is how long we're allowed to discuss strategy. Once the timer runs out, the person whose turn it is does whatever they want and we're not allowed to argue about it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: The problem with this game is that the challenge is hugely variable from one game to the next. This is because you are essentially playing against a stack of shuffled cards, and any given card you draw might scupper your plans completely or do absolutely nothing depending on the board state. The game shines when you are lucky enough to get a good balance - a game where you win or lose by a tiny margin at the 11th hour - and every card draw brings enormous tension. But half the time you will either stomp the game and win without any real difficulty, or the game will stomp you and leave you feeling rather dissatisfied. The game actually has a mechanism aimed at preventing this imbalance, which distributes the dangerous cards somewhat evenly in the main stack so you won't draw 3/4 of them when you're only 1/4 of the way through the game, but that has the unfortunate effect of making it too predictable sometimes.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Another game that got a rare 7 rating from me after one play.  Actually, after 3 plays, because we played it three times the first time I played it.  Update: after those first 3 plays, it took over a year to play again.  The 4th game was in May 2009.  Once people started bringing it to CABS (and then CABS got its own copy), it became a dime (10+ plays) in 2009.  Update several years later: I've now played it a lot and I have my own copy.  I still like it a lot, but it does seem to be more susceptible to "one player dominates the game" than other cooperative games.  Especially when you play with open cards, as we do.  But if you have closed hands, players are still allowed to talk about them, so it slows the game way down as people talk about their hands to excess.  It's best with new players who don't mind a little coaching or players of roughly equal experience who aren't afraid to give as good as they get.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Being able to use drawn cards to either enable passing of other cards or cleanup (by travelling) or directly for finding a cure makes for an interesting tension and decisions.

The various abilities give each player a specialised role and working out how best to exploit everybody's skills is the main issue. This keeps the game exciting - I felt everybody was involved even outside their turn, since so much co-operation was truly needed.

Lost 2x. 2nd time may have been a win if we'd realised players could use action points to GET cards.

Losing by so little (and feeling that we had made genuine mistakes earlier on) meant everyone was ready to play it again soon. 

I can imagine the game losing a lot of its charm when it's been 'solved' and failure rests more upon luck than any mistakes. Until then, though, it's a 9.1. I'm curious to see how easily the other role-combinations will be solved after one has been.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Excellent game. Even on lower difficulties, I've rarely had a winning game where victory wasn't coming down to the wire. Seriously, games are always close when you win. When you lose - it's possible to lose horribly and you can only laugh when the game really screws you over! :)

My only quibble with this type of co-op game is that it is common to breed a table captain. Then it just becomes a single player game, with one player telling everyone else where to move. I try hard to avoid that, as the more experienced player I find it better just to advise others what their character can do ability wise and then let them lead the discussion on their own turn.

The board and components are of nice quality. Artwork is all excellent. Game mechanics and turn structure are simple to learn but can offer great depth.

All in all, games are generally a fun, exciting and engrossing experience. I really recommend Pandemic.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is a great co-op game of solving a puzzle like problem. You need to coordinate with your teammates to maximize individual character abilities and win the game by curing 4 diseases. Suspend reality, and treat the game for what it is, a co-op puzzle, and you will enjoy it. It is easy to get it up and running and it will be a constant go to for an easy and fun game. You can also make it more difficult by adding extra "bad" cards into the deck as your skills increase. It is also a good solo game.

On the other hand, if you are a hardcore gamer who wants depth, competition and a significant challenge from a game, Pandemic is not your game. I use it in my high school science classroom, not for its science, but for cooperative learning, problem solving, and communication. For that ... that game works very well. But this is not a game I am going to take out and play unless I am playing with neophyte gamers.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Early when I was starting my gaming collection, this seemed like it should be an auto include.  Everyone online loved it and said it was a great way to get people into gaming.

I was a bit disappointed with it.  My wife and I enjoyed it the first few times we played it, but after you know what to do, everything just becomes automatic and either it works out or it doesn't.  Sometimes the order of the cards is just too cruel and you cannot win, but often just doing the obvious things to do gets you there.

Pandemic also suffers from what I generally dislike in cooperative games.  The guy who owns the game and explains it to everyone knows how to win.  So he gets put in the awkward situation of telling everyone how to win or letting them fend for themselves and watch as the game implodes.  Neither option is very fun for me, and none of our games have ended with "Wow, that was a lot of fun!  Let's play again!".
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Now that I have played Pandemic: Reign of Cthulhu, I see why this had to exist: as a seed that would one day sprout into a better game.

This really isn't bad. The theme works, and even though it uses the dreaded, fun-killing cubes, it does feel like a plague is relentlessly spreading across the globe. With the variety of roles, replayability is strong. And it's fun, despite the grim subject matter that feels even grimmer today.

But after about 10 plays, including two or three with my young son, I found I'd had enough. There was always an optimal move (and if you didn't see it, somebody else would.)  It was a bit procedural and dry. And it didn't have the kind of emergent narrative that would make me want to play it 20 or 50 or 100 times.

So it moved on, along with my unplayed copy of On the Brink, in a trade for something else. I don't remember what I got, but I have never regretted parting with it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
There is a tremendous amount of unavoidable randomness. I prefer games to end with the feeling, "I wish I had done this differently," but every game of Pandemic merely ends with, "I wish this had happened differently." Whether it's drawing two epidemics in a row, having an immediate unavoidable outbreak following an epidemic, or having all of the cards of a certain color at the bottom of a deck -- there's just so many factors which can lead to a game loss being completely out of your control.

Besides that, the amount of agency each player has on the game is practically zero. You can go for a 15 minute smoke break and come back and see what players have decided for you to do on your turn. Perhaps in this way it's a "true cooperative" game, in the same way Solitaire could be a true cooperative game. But I strongly prefer cooperative games like Hanabi where players are forced to make their own decisions.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
July 28, 2008 -- I was introduced to this last week, and in one session I played four games of it. I was pleasantly surprised to find the game is fun, requires a fair bit of thought and is not easy for the players to win. Its quick play time makes it a clear winner. I must buy this. 9/10

January 15, 2010 -- After eight plays, I finally experienced a win. It was close. We were down to our last turn of drawing cards into our hands, so the time limit was just about to kill us. It was a three-player game, and we had done quite well keeping outbreaks from happening with any great frequency. We'd just barely pushed the Infection Rate to 4. With the medic, researcher and scientist, we barely beat the clock.

I find Pandemic continues to be tense and interesting. Now that my girlfriend has experienced its fun and is asking to play it, I expect it to hit the table a lot more often.

No change in rating. 9/10
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Its fast and tense and the teamwork is a lot of fun (with the right people). Sometimes a session quickly turns hopeless but at least its easy to restart. Probably not for eurosnoots or those who think the height of boardgaming is Monopoly. I must get a copy of this one if for no other reason than to lure potential geeks into the hobby. I can see this game being easily modified with custom rules, especially the role cards.

>>Am getting a bit lukewarm about this game. The mechanics are brilliant and there is good tension in the game. The main drawback is that it is prone to alpha gamer (mainly due to their superior experience) making most of the important decisions, overtly or otherwise, leaving less dominant players or newbies with little or no meaningful role (which might be perfectly OK for some groups). As such, its collaborative but not quite. On the Brink, with the terrorist, fixes this problem.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
2013-02-27
With a group that works together (even if debating the best course of action), this game is incredible. Every card draw is tense and every move walks the fine line between success and failure. Defeat encourages you to try again; victory encourages you to see if you can keep the streak going. I played this 7 times in two days with the same group, and we never got tired of it.

2013-09-02
After having a lot of plays in just a few other co-op games, I can see that there is much less cooperation involved in Pandemic. Yes, each player has their own specialized roles that help the group, but the only thing that can be accomplished on your own is removing disease cubes (a minor task, overall). Because of this, the game doesn't come down to working together so much as putting everyone's ideas to a vote. I have to lower my rating from a 9 to a 6, since it's no longer my first choice in co-op games.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Cooperative game where every player has a unique character with unique capabilities that have to work together (really together, almost no mistake is allowed) in order to defeat the spreading of illness. The game is easy to explain, the idea is very good, I think that the mechanics are may be too general and can be applied to other games (forbidden island for instant, very similar), but the game is fun to play. The biggest issue that I have is that, for me, this game is, in reality, a solitaire game. The complexity is so high that, in the end, one player has to control almost everything in order to succeed.
Positive:
1. High complexity. When you win, there is a real feeling of victory
2. Easy to explain
3. The actions are easy, the difficulty lies in how to combine them
4. Quick to play and quick set up
Negative:
1. More suitable for 1 player
2. The best version, for me, is the digital one (tablet)
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: This game is a classic!  This game is always an option to play on game night for our group!  A stand-out among other cooperative board games, the mechanics of Pandemic produces such dramatic effects (especially towards the end of the game), it's as if the game is itself another player working against the rest of the group!  Cooperation and coordination are essential for this game, as well as intimate knowledge of the game mechanics.  The simulation of the 4 diseases spreading across the globe is particularly creative.  The random elements and the combination of roles create significant replay value.  Because Pandemic allows multiple avenues to winning the game, I really enjoy playing this game with different groups, who approach the challenges in this game differently.  Pandemic is a unique and entertaining experience that will remain a staple in the collection of table top games for generations!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Easy to learn, attractive components, but lacking in interesting strategy decisions.  Luck sometimes overshadows skill - the game should come with a built in system to warn players when no conceivable combination of plays can prevent defeat.  Sometimes you just can't win no matter what you do; other games will be won even with mediocre play; sometimes winning is possible only with good play.  The games of the first kind are frustrating and unsatisfactory because your time is wasted; games of the the second kind are boring because winning is too easy; only games of the third kind provide satisfaction by rewarding skillful play.  In all, I feel my time is better spent playing other games.  Rating based on three plays at the introductory level of difficulty and two plays at normal level of difficulty.  Rating of 5.33 is composite of my rating (4), my wife's rating (6) and my sister's rating (6).
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
The game is so easy to teach and play. It is tense and animated. I like the outbreak mechanic. I also like how each combination of characters abilities make the game ever green. You can tweak the difficulty to your liking.
On the downside, (1) sometimes it can feel like cleaning the board of little glass cubes, rather than eradicating diseases. (2) I don't really understand how collecting city cards help you cure a disease, from a thematic stand point. (3) it can get very hard with 4 players, which is a shame, as it is only then that you get the full collaborative experience and synergies between characters. (4) the only mechanic to slow down alpha players is that you are not meant to show your cards, which arguably isn't really enough to stop those players. (5) Luck does play a big role in your success or failure. There is no morale choice to make, all choices are related to risk management.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
31-10-2015. Rated after 1 play. So I finally played Pandemic. It's really, really close to something like Defenders of the Realm. I'm not sure what I like better, the lean design of Pandemic or the Fluff of DotR.

Regardless. Pandemic is a coop game set in a diseased planet Earth, where massive disease outbreaks need to be controlled by a team of medical doctors.

Each turn, each player has 4 action points to spend. By spending the points. These points you use to travel to locations, cure disease cubes, build CDC centers etcetera. At the end of your turn, you flip and resolve 2 cards that repopulate the board with disease. If there ever a 4th cube placed in a city of 1 disease, the disease has an outbreak and spreads to adjacent cities.

You win as soon as you develop a cure for the diseases in the game, and you discard a card by tossing 5 location cards while balancing the board for disease.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I definately enjoy  this game's version of coop play.  More so than in other coops I feel like this game can really go bad for you and its not through sub-optimal play.  Actions are always tight and you always wish you had just one more.  The different roles really maximize replayability and definately chang up the strategies.  Components are good if not great and are really added to by purchasing a petree dish for each cube color.  The game is definately easier with less players.  I've lost severl 4 player games (w/ 5 Epidemics) but the balance still felt right and the tension was always there.  If you drop down to 3 players I think you need a 6th epidemic to make it more tense.

textfield_comment_value:
Original comment:
Fascinating mechanics and structure. I don't know yet if the "rigging" of the infections as to target the already-sick cities tips the game too much in the too-hard-to-win direction. But it's fun trying to win so far, and it's one of the only quick cooperative games out there, and could be used to introduce casual gamers into more strategic fare.

Years later:
IMO, Forbidden Desert upgraded this game in almost every way. It removes the finicky setup, removes the likelihood of a quick death by insta-Outbreaks amongst your first cities that got 3 cubes on them to start, and does everything Pandemic does but does it better, and cheaper.

Pandemic was a fantastic entry into the co-operative gaming genre, and simultaneously revolutionized and popularized it, but the years have passed it by (base game) as the designer's sequels surpassed the original in every way I care about.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
One of a couple games that Katie and I have wildly varied opinions on.  This was one of our first cooperative games and I enjoyed it quite a bit at first.  As time has gone on though, I now find it rather dull.  It seems, from the games we have played, that there must be an extensive amount of discussion and debate on who should do what in order to be successful in this game, and that causes the game to drag on much longer than it ought to.  I have found that I would rather rush through this game and lose than draw it out for a long while and win.  I'm also not a big fan of the board and components.  Ironically, I quite enjoyed the variants introduced with Pandemic's expansion pack, but Katie and others have not.  In the end, when it comes to fighting cooperatively against wooden cubes, I much prefer Flash Point over Pandemic.

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Highly strategic. Short playtime. My favorite part is the planning on how to utilize each role's ability to get the most out of the next set of moves for all characters. For me however, the base game is very limiting with just 7 possible roles. To make the game more replayable and exciting, new role cards from the expansions could be used for a wider range of abilities. After winning the different challenges, I sold the game as I don't think there is anything left for me to prove on the game. But if anyone asks me to play it with them, I'd gladly join :)

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Addictive game. Definitely my wife's favorite new game in a long time, and since it plays so well with two it has quickly jumped towards the top of my most played list in a very short amount of time. Maybe 3 other games in my game playing career have been played so often so quickly (Lost Cities, Settlers, Race for the Galaxy). However, while it is a very good game, I can't bring myself to call it one of my own faves. I keep fearing I'm playing it wrong because I have beaten it all but once out of almost 10 times, including a couple on "Heroic"...not only winning them but winning most of them without as much tension as I would like. I want to feel like I barely eak out a win. Still, there are times the game is gloriously nail-biting, and the mechanics are very cool and the theme sounds a bit strange but it's uniqueness and "real world setting" make it really stand out as a winner.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Considered to be a very good co-op board game, I find this to be a bit like Solitaire where it's really the game letting you win by the distribution of infected cities at the startand the game not giving you a lot of epidemic cards in a row. There is a difficulty setting that can be adjusted (altered by inserting more or less Epidemic cards), but it seems a little futile sometimes. What I don't really like in the mechanics of the game, I do like in the theme of the game. It simulates spread of disease well and realistically and sometimes you just can't control the random events of what happens. Everyone gets their own special role and can contribute in their own way. It forces communication, but doesn't rid the problem of the overbearing co-op teammate. Overally, I like Pandemic, but not a game to play regularly. It is a good game to start other players on. Best played with 4 or 5
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Great theme for a coop game and particularly well integrated into the game. Tough decisions to be made throughout the game. Nice buildup to a climax as the game always seems to be close. There are no shortcuts or easy ways to win this one unless you get very lucky. Very easy to adapt for solo play and the short playing time is a bonus also. 

After a few more plays it seems that the challenges presented aren't the same for different player numbers. The difficulty remains the same but when playing with a lower number of players the problem is managing the outbreaks where with more players the problems seems to be to discover the cures. Interesting design!

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Great cooperative game, with lots of tension, and very scalable (though I must mention that number of players influences the difficulty, with 2p being the easiest). It's funny for both casual and experienced players.

The deck reseeding mechanic triggered by epidemic cards, causing cities to be infected again and again, is one of the most brilliant mechanics in the whole boardgame world.

One of the most intriguing aspects of Pandemic is the pace of the game: the tension grows with the increasing number of outbreaks, while players race to find the cures, and the finale is often very climatic (even when losing)!

Pandemic is hands down the best cooperative game around (said by a guy that's not in love with coops), with the possible exception of Space Alert (that is on a league of its own, being an ingenious out of the norm design, and that's definitely more a gamers' game...)!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
A solid game that I am usually willing to play, but one that has never (and likely will never) sucked me in. I wish I could love it instead of like it, but it's simply too obvious. Odd choice of words? Let me explain. Pandemic has a very clear turn order, and it becomes obvious what MUST be done on every turn. If one deviates from this, if one, in essence, chooses to play the game his/her own way, the game could very well be lost. Not my idea of fun. With Defenders of the Realm or Arkham, for example, a certain degree of failure is accounted for due to the randomness associated with the game. I prefer that sense of freedom and variability.

EDIT: 12/30/12
Just got back from a vacation where I had the opportunity to play this with a few kids (13-16). I'm bumping the score a half a point after seeing how great this game works with non-gamers. Finally found a solid use for it.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Played the boardgame once, was told what to do by the game owner. Typical boring alpha player co-op, and very dry, lacking theme, mechanics have no relation to theme or reality. "I'll give you this research data on Lagos but only if we both travel to Lagos first and are there at the same time." What? Is this game set in 1930?

Bought the app to give it a second chance, which allowed me to control four characters and play solitaire, quickly. Became obvious game is random garbage. First game, I lost on the second turn. Second game, I lost on the first turn, before two of my characters even got their first turn. Never seen a design so flawed before. A game where a player can lose before they even get to go?

The kind of game that makes you remember that other people's criteria for a good game can be quite different from your own. 

Would never play the physical game again.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: I had Pandemic a long time ago within a year of its release.  I thought it was okay but not great and sold it.  Since then Pandemic has become so popular that I end up playing it every year somehow even though I always think of it as tremendously overrated.  I've come around to it partially.  Pandemic is an elegant game with a cool theme that fits.  The theme comes through but it's not as if it is the focus of the game.  There's perhaps a story but it takes some imagination.  After a while it feels more like an abstract puzzle.  I think this is also very prone to an alpha player.  Ideally there's lots of teamwork and discussion, at worst one person is playing it solitairre telling everyone what do do.  That's not a problem unique to pandemic but with most co-ops.  I am interested to try the legacy version though because I think more of a story would really help this.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I will readily admit that I am very partial to cooperative games.  I love the idea of working together as a team to defeat the game.  And this is the most streamlined cooperative game I have ever seen.  Many groups will argue that it is not enjoyable because one person can control the game and tell others what to do.  While this is possible, our group just doesn't work that way.

For me it's almost like a brainstorming session.  People look at their cards and they throw out ideas for what they could do.  The key to the game is allowing all the players to contribute and make their own final decisions.  I love the ebb-and-flow of the diseases in this game.  The way that the disease can be under control and then one epidemic later things are a nightmare again.  We have a fairly good success rate with 5 epidemics, but we usually win with only 1 turn left in the game.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
The idea of this game is awesome. Cooperating with your friends to rid the world of disease sounds like my kind of game. And to top it all off, every player has their own special skills to contribute to the team. I love it.

The thing that makes this game not fun are players like myself. I am a total Dictator. I'm the person who introduced the game to my friends and so automatically I fell into the teaching role, but, there's a fine line between teacher and dictator. I cross that line. I spend all game telling people what to do. Before people even take their turn I'm giving them "suggestions" and when they don't follow my "suggestions" I tell them how inefficient their turn was and how we will all fail because of them. I should just play this game solo. 

There needs to be some sort of rule or mechanic that prevents people like me from controlling the entire game.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I’ve always thought that cooperative games were kind of dull, but this is a really fun one. This is an efficiency game, where you try to do as much in as little time as possible. You have to deal with immediate threats, but you also have a long term goal. The players form a team in contrary to Lord of the rings and Shadows over Camelot which feels more solitaire and try to cure the diseases. I have played several games where there has been tension to the end. It plays in a quite short amount of time, which is good. After a few plays moves become predictable and you need the expansion to stir things up.

I have played it with two, three and four (and with the expansion five) players. With two players I think it were a little easier than three, but that might depend on the pair of roles I got, but it worked otherwise equally good.

Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Your team of experts must prevent the world from succumbing to a viral pandemic.

* Played
- 2-4 Players (Best: 4)
- Cooperative game
- Playtime: 45 min
- Normal setup
- Several virulent diseases have broken out simultaneously all over the world! The players are disease-fighting specialists whose mission is to treat disease hotspots while researching cures for each of four plagues before they get out of hand.
The game board depicts several major population centers on Earth. On each turn, a player can use up to four actions to travel between cities, treat infected populaces, discover a cure, or build a research station. A deck of cards provides the players with these abilities, but sprinkled throughout this deck are Epidemic! cards that accelerate and intensify the diseases' activity. A second, separate deck of cards controls the "normal" spread of the infections.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Rating 4 based on: 
5 - Average game...
3 - ...Likely won't play this again although could be convinced...

My Thoughts: 
I don't get the praise for this game, maybe it deserved it at the time it came out but there are so many better options now. It's a pretty standard pure co-op game which falls victim to everyone having to follow the optimal strategy once it becomes apparent, which takes away your agency as a player and doesn't allow you to make interesting choices unless you want to screw everyone over. It also just doesn't have the fun factor. I believe that a good co-op game should always have hidden information so your choice is always your own with a few exceptions like Eldritch Horror (though I would love to see a version of that with a hidden cultist role). And for a light pure co-op experience that's fun I'd stick to the forbidden series of co-op games.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
In Pandemic, several virulent diseases have broken out simultaneously all over the world! The players are disease-fighting specialists whose mission is to treat disease hotspots while researching cures for each of four plagues before they get out of hand.

Taking a unique role within the team, players must plan their strategy to mesh with their specialists' strengths in order to conquer the diseases. For example, the Operations Expert can build research stations which are needed to find cures for the diseases and which allow for greater mobility between cities; the Scientist needs only four cards of a particular disease to cure it instead of the normal five—but the diseases are spreading quickly and time is running out. If one or more diseases spreads beyond recovery or if too much time elapses, the players all lose. If they cure the four diseases, they all win!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
A cooperative game that takes the best of other games and throws out the useless bits. Where Kniza's LOTR is overly fiddly (too many paths), this one streamlines it (players use 4APs to perform actions). Where games like Terra had too much infighting, this one forces players to fully cooperate as there is a sense of urgency.

The outbreak system works well and so do the role cards. The game will probably get a little stale after you manage to win it on heroic and also because strategies will become more obvious after multiple plays...BUT it will take awhile to get there!

We played three games of this in a row and it has been awhile since a game made me jump up with excitement.

Update: Game gets stale after beating it a few times. Some roles are stronger than others and the theme is thin once people get into a 'system' of trying best to solve the puzzle.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
This is a hit with my girlfriend because of the cooperative play. We are often playing 2 player games; she can be a sore loser if I beat her badly or frequently. Consequently, she'll only play strategy games with me to keep me happy, but I can tell she would rather not.

This game on the other hand she's happy to play. She doesn't mind losing if we're doing it together. We spent a whole night playing this game with thriller/suspense Quarantine type movies playing in the background. She was suggesting we play another game for once, instead of me. 

Your success/demise is sometimes inevitable based on the card shuffle, but it really is a well balanced game. So while there are a few hopeless situations, most of the time you at least feel like you had a chance -- if only a couple things went your way at the end. 

The different player roles add much needed variety.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Had this in my collection for a while before I finally broke it out for a solo round. Before long, those solo rounds almost became a nightly activity and before even longer, got it to the family table. 

Wow! This one is about as streamlined as they come. The cooperation, actions, decision-making and options all are creative, simple and extremely engaging. Pandemic is the easiest game I have to set up and take down and can fit on my own computer desk. It is inexpensive (compared to most games) and has a tremendous theme. I'm tired of generic fantasy and dungeon-esque paper mache. I wish more games were this well-rounded and amazing. 

My only quibbles is that this can be tense, sometimes difficult to win and, most unshockingly, be an AG's stomping ground. Active participation and suggestions are key but let players decide for themselves in the end. Jus' sayin.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
El juego es un Excelente Cooperativo, de hecho es en mi parecer “El Cooperativo”, si nunca has tenido una experiencia con un juego cooperativo este introduce unas mecánicas ideales para el jugador principiante, mas no deja a un lado el jugador experimentando donde las dificultades que propone el juego son todo un reto, no es fácil de ganar y es un verdadero reto al jugar solo dos personas con un solo personaje, o con más de 5 cartas.

Estéticamente el juego tiene una producción muy buena cuidando con mucha meticulosidad los detalles, y los componentes para una persona nueva en el tema de los juegos de mesa resultan bastante bonitos.

Como apreciación personal este fue mi primer juego de mesa más de “especialista”, además de los típicos juegos familiares. A mi esposa y a mí nos encantó y gracias a él decidimos entrar en el mundo de los juegos de mesa de lleno.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Update after a few solo games on iOS
As a solo game (which, for me, is the only way most cooperative games should be played), this rates at least a 6.


----
A quick-playing cooperative game. Sometimes it's quick because it's impossible to solve! A fun activity, but more like a group puzzle than a game. It has the same silly rule as Lord of the Rings: players may share ANY information freely, but may not actually show each other their cards. I MUCH prefer Shadows Over Camelot. However, this game does have an interesting theme, plays very quickly, and has a very clever way of mimicking disease spread. It's also scalable, similar to Vanished Planet (add more Epidemic cards to the deck to increase difficulty). Players MUST work together -- each character's power can be helpful if used correctly.

But I don't like co-ops! For me, this is a 3/10 on the BGG scale.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Since co-op games are a little odd, my rating is basically relative to LotR or SoC. Pandemic scores against these by having a more interesting theme, and requiring more movement in gameplay. LotR feels like walking down a road. SoC often feels like "I'll go over here and hang around for a few turns". Pandemic requires you to buzz around prioritising your actions; acquiring the cards to discover a series of cures while fire-fighting outbreaks. And all the while the clock is ticking. First four plays gave a couple of close wins (one turn from losing), and a spectacularly dreadful 17-minute loss when we failed to get to grips with an unlucky S.America setup. And we haven't moved beyond the beginers version yet. Very clever infection deck mechanism to re-infect locations.

Update: Rating reduced because after the first 5 plays, nobody has asked to play again.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
The cooperative game that made cooperative games a thing and yet it holds up amidst the slew of games that copied it.  I don't understand why more games don't copy the best part of this system--the shuffling of the epidemics and infection cards so that players always have a rough sense of the probability of all possible negative events.  This means the tension between trying to achieve victory and avoid failure blends with constantly shifting risk assessment.  Every decision is meaningful but the outcomes are not deterministic.  

I also enjoy the logistics puzzle of optimizing movement and the multi-use cards.  Although the theme has become more painful recently, I still appreciate how the game celebrates scientists and medical personnel.  I've played this with doctors and a CDC researcher (pre-pandemic) and they always appreciate the theme quite a bit.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
[b]Positive points[/b]:
• Great buildup of tension as the game progresses
• While there is some thematic randomness, certain elements can be anticipated and you can potentially prepare for them when they come around again
• Potentially soloable, if you don't mind playing without any hidden information

[b]Negative points[/b]:
• There really isn't much you can do out-of-turn unless you're actively helping with strategy
• While thematic, your actions aren't the most exciting and not always particularly satisfying either

[b]To note[/b]:
• Arguably some role combinations work better than others
• How much hidden information between the players is up to you which can incidentally make things easier or more challenging
• Decision making is mostly tactical and reactive; any attempt at coming up with some come of strategy can be potentially disrupted by infections
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
It might be a little too much of a co-operative game for my tastes, but I guess it just adds to the all-for-one atmosphere.  I'm starting to think it's impossible to win, but I think a lot of that is the element of luck involved in the drawing of cards.  I tend to like the fact that it's unpredictable, but I think some would dislike that.  Whatever...I'd rather have a game that's too hard than one that's too easy.

I think this game is almost played out for me.  Just won a five-player, six epidemic game fairly handily.  Still fun, but wouldn't be my first choice of a game at this point.

Taught a group of eleven year-olds this game and they absolutely loved it.  They really enjoyed the team aspect of it; they found the experience of working together in a board game very unique and different from what they were had previously experienced.

(wife rating: 9)
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Copycat purchase.  many plays prior to joining BGG. after many competetive games of catan, carcassonne etc, tempers wouldn't necessarily flare but we needed something to take the edge off competition, so here comes pandemic.  still a very good game.  challenging and tense and things can spiral out of controll very quickly.  we have gravitated to having favored roles so many times we just pick who we want to play, sometimes have a random draw.  we like to cooperative aspect and has lead to purchases of mice & mystics, star trek expeditions, yggdrasil and a touch of evil(which can be competitve or cooperative).  so it opened a new world of gaming, the cooperative idea.  haven'f felt the need for the expansion since we haven't mastered the base game with all epidemics yet.  kids have grown into liking this as well so it will be well loved for many years yet.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Very good.  The mechanisms work in an interesting way to present you with a real challenge - so much so that in our first game we were badly beaten.  But the game was still so appealing that we all wanted to play again immediately and this time we won - though not without teetering on the edge of disaster before doing so - which made victory all the sweeter.  Having the medic in play the second time seemed to make things easier, though we also worked together better. Looking forward to another go but finding it hard to envisage how you can win on anything other than the easy setting!  Further play makes the medic look essential and even easy look hard.  We seem a long way from heroic!  Further plays help, as experience helps you better exploit the benefits of co-operation - still not easy though.  

On the Brink is a nice addition - see comments there.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
A classic game that I feel grew a bit long in the tooth as the system kept being reapplied to new versions. From what I have heard the legacy versions are the "final form" of pandemic style game.

From my perspective these games all share the same Achilles heel. There is so many ways to lose the game by not capitalizing on the most efficient moves each turn that the game incentives back seat gaming.

Almost every game of this I have played has devolved into the most experienced player instructing everyone else or everyone's character is played by committee if players are equally skilled. 

his means that less experienced players often feel shut out of the decisions making progress unless you take steps to not influence them, which will drastically reduce your chances of winning

Still it is ranked 97 for a reason and will provide many hours of fun play.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Pandemic es mi primer juego colaborativo. Al principio hay que leer con detenimiento el manual para poder empezar a jugar sin caer en ambigüedades. La mecánica es un tanto difícil de asimilar al principio, pero cuando has jugado unas cuantas partidas te haces con ella. Tiene 3 niveles de dificultad que se determinan por el número de epidemias: 4, 5 o 6. Cada jugador lleva un personaje que tiene habilidades especiales. Es muy importante conocerlas bien para poder coordinarte con tus compañeros y tratar de ganar al juego. En cada turno puedes hacer hasta 4 acciones, que pueden ser muy diversas, y dependerán del escenario que se esté presentando. Las alternativas son múltiples, pero conviene mantener mucho diálogo con tus compañeros para conseguir la mejor estrategia conjunta. Me gusta mucho Pandemic porque requiere de mucha interacción con los compañeros.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is really good those first handful of games you play for sure. Tension, learning what to prioritize, getting lucky draws, tension again--it's all good stuff. Importantly, it's beatable. Being a family game, the necessity of the game to retain as much of traditional board game mechanics is paramount, and that includes victory being almost thrust at players once they understand it.

That does, however, mean the game quickly gets very tedious. Victory becomes something that feels uncontrolled; it doesn't feel like it is up to you whether you win or lose. Tweaking the formula to suit your skill level only changes the outcome, not the strategy nor the pace.

If you enjoy the game for your first 5 or 10 plays, don't wait for it to get stale. Go right out and grab an expansion. Any of them will inject more stressful decisions and stronger mechanics.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
In this cooperative game, players take on the role of medic, researcher, operations expert, dispatcher or scientist to combat 4 different diseases affecting the world. Players have 4 actions on their turn, to move, build research station, slow the disease or find a cure. Epidemics can break out and spread around the world. An excellent, fast paced game. A realistic mechanic is where the diseased cities are shuffled back in to the top of the epidemic pile. You feel like you are running around, with hardly any time. 

This is a very fun, addictive game. You keep wanting to play, to improve your play, and win. A side note, our gaming group has three copies of the game, and two of the games have duplicate cards. One of the games has a duplicate Khartoum infection card, and another game has a duplicate Los Angeles draw deck. Check your copy to be sure!
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
You are specialists at the CDC/Atlanta where you watch several virulent diseases break out simultaneously all over the world. The team mission is to prevent a worldwide pandemic outbreak, treating hot spots while researching cures for each of the four plagues before they get out of hand.

Players must plan their strategy to mesh their specialists' strengths before the diseases overwhelm the world. For example, the Operations Expert can build research stations which are needed to find cures for the diseases. The Scientist needs only 4 cards of a particular disease to cure it instead of the normal 5. But the diseases are breaking out fast and time is running out: the team must try to stem the tide of infection in diseased areas while developing cures. If disease spreads uncontrolled, the players all lose. If they can cure all four diseases, they win.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I have only one game under my belt, so take all this for what it's worth.

I've played all the major co-op games on the market (Lord of the Rings, Shadows over Camelot, Battlestar Galactica, and now Pandemic). Of those games, Pandemic is probably the simplest design and the easiest to understand. This is a good thing. My friend (who brought the game) plays regularly with his children, which is a Good Thing.

At the same time, I think I prefer the linearity of Lord of the Rings over Pandemic. I think this is because I prefer the sense of handling this particular obstacle (a given board in LotR) then the firefighting of Pandemic.

I also didn't find Pandemic to be nearly as gut-wrenching as other co-ops. I don't know why. Maybe world-threatening diseases don't trip my trigger as much as destroying The One Ring or shepherding the human race to Kobol.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
I really enjoyed the cooperative nature of the game. With a group of people that can get overly competitive when playing each other, it's fun that the game receives other players frustrations. 

Pandemic manages to keep you at least slightly on edge the entire game. By the time you work your way through curing a couple of diseases, the others may be quite out of hand, which ups the excitement and certainly makes you consider how to play the game better the next time. 

The only downside I noticed was that each person has ideas on the best way to win, or even how to make a move during their turn. If there is at least 1 player with strong opinions, you may end up dealing with tension between players. But, that's a great opportunity to work on communication! 

Pandemic skillfully stresses while providing an exciting challenge for you and your friends.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value:
Would have rated this a 10 when we first got it. A very fun puzzle where chaos can break out at any point and good strategy is rewarded. Throw in an interesting and well-done theme, plus cooperative, and it's a winner. 

I'll temper that by saying that once you sort of "figure it out," the initial burst of excitement can fade. It's still fun and becomes light for experienced players, but there will be less tension once you've seen everything the game has to offer. To counter this stalled-out feeling, it sounds like the Pandemic franchise has done a great job with expansions and spin-off games, and I'm excited to try some of those.  

EDIT: My wife and I keep coming back to this game. We've kept it fresh by doing a couple campaigns, and even after all our plays, I still find it thrilling. 10/10 for this being one of our most beloved, enduring games.
Title: Pandemic

textfield_comment_value: Overall good game. It can be easy if four players get the scientist, researcher, dispatcher, and Organizer. However, you can get wrecked pretty quick if there's back to back pandemic cards drawn, which causes outbreaks on cities you just hit and then a whole chain happens (to which, little you can do) and then the cubes run out. Bam done. Happened two games in a row. Yes we shuffled the deck but I guess there's that odd chance that the last card in one deck and the first in the next can be pandemic cards, and those cities could have 5 others connected (using up more cubes). Apart from helpless frustration at times, it is a fun game. It's cool to work together to beat the game. You feel accomplished when you beat it. But this game doesn't seem super special to me, I couldn't see giving it more than an 8.5 but I will change score after more plays.

Update July 2017
Haven't played this in over 15 years, but revisited it and some modern variants in the past year or so, including Cthulhu and Iberia. I really liked it way back when it was one of the first co-ops to appear on the scene. Nowadays I feel like the mechanisms are too artificial...or perhaps the nature of the mechanisms feel obtrusive, less integrated into the theme than could be. I may have been spoiled by Burgle Bros. In any case, I feel like my tastes have changed and the Pandemic mechanisms don't hold up well for me.

Every turn the disease's growth, and can make a lot of disasters. Your team has to make quick decisions to don't let the diseases go out of control (outbreak), growth more than can be cured or be late. All of those 3 points are the way your team can lose.

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic is a great design no matter what people think and say. It is a really simple design, that is easy to play, explain, and understand the game state at any given time. If it was because of that alone I would give it a 10 because it needs to be acknowledged. 
I enjoy the puzzle very much, and different character combinations make it slightly different every time, though the base game can grow stall and deterministic as you learn to play the game. It's a really good intro to board games, a game that doesn't overstay its welcome, and that is universally liked, except for those who already know how to play it well.

I wouldn't go to a board game night because Pandemic is getting played, but if it got picked, I wouldn't disagree and if it helps other people discover modern boardgames for the first time, then please count me in for another ride

textfield_comment_value:
Pandemic ranks as perhaps the best game I have ever played. The basic rules are elegant and intuitive, the cooperative format is welcoming and friendly, and the roughly 90-minute play time all make the game extremely approachable and convenient. Elements of randomness never feel as though they override good strategy, but demand that those strategies constantly adapt to the changing situation. The difficulty is also quite high, but is widely adjustable (especially with the various expansion components) and ensures that even experienced teams will never find the game trivial. 

Exceptional!

textfield_comment_value:
The game that popularized co-ops.  Extremely accessible and engaging, with a serious theme that appeals to many "non-gamers".

Yes, if player skill differs widely, Pandemic can suffer from the "director" issue, but I don't see that as a fundamental flaw: almost all strategy games suffer when played with players of widely differing skill levels.  Singling out this issue in co-op games while not acknowledging it in competitive games is disingenuous.

(Truth in advertising: I playtested Pandemic, added 2 roles and rewrote its rules for 2nd Edition, and co-authored its expansions.)

This one can definitely give you an ulcer!

textfield_comment_value:
2-4 Players

In Pandemic, several virulent diseases have broken out simultaneously all over the world! The players are disease-fighting specialists whose mission is to treat disease hotspots while researching cures for each of four plagues before they get out of hand.

The game board depicts several major population centers on Earth. On each turn, a player can use up to four actions to travel between cities, treat infected populaces, discover a cure, or build a research station. A deck of cards provides the players with these abilities, but sprinkled throughout this deck are Epidemic! cards that accelerate and intensify the diseases' activity. A second, separate deck of cards controls the "normal" spread of the infections.

textfield_comment_value: Pandemic works very well thematically speaking and it is a great introduction to cooperative games. What is particularly clever is how the game scales with different player count: with more players, there will be more "infect cities" phases and the draw deck will run out sooner, however, you will have more specialist powers and more players to reach the number of cards needed for discovering a cure. The asymmetric player powers are very well designed and make each game a bit different, depending on your own role and the combination of characters. In general, I now consider the game a gateway game, which is why it left my collection.
